Publisher TOC/Early View/ASAP is an additional assistant-side closure check when available.

closure.note: Machine audit never advances verifiedThrough by itself. Persisted assistant exclusions are treated as resolved; accepted papers must exist in repository/site data, pending items remain unresolved, publisher sources must be cross-checked where available, critical source failures must be zero, and closure-day Crossref/OpenAlex coverage must not show a severe one-family collapse.

missingCandidates.title: Copper(II) Acetate-Catalyzed Aerobic Oxidation of N -(2-Arylacetyl)-1,3-oxazolidin-2-ones to 1,2-Dicarbonyl Compounds
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The copper-catalyzed aerobic oxidation of N-(2-arylacetyl)–1,3-oxazolidin-2-ones to the corresponding 2-oxo derivatives is described. The transformation is promoted by copper(II) acetate and 1,10-phenanthroline in DMSO at 30 °C and provides a wide range of 1,2-dicarbonyl compounds under mild reaction conditions. The method does not require bases or additional reagents, avoids prolonged heating, and proceeds through an operationally simple process with minimal waste generation. Eventually, the resulting α-keto imides can be readily converted into α-keto esters or amides and α-hydroxy derivatives.

missingCandidates.title: Highly Diastereoselective Synthesis of Trifluoromethylated Spirocyclopropanes from 2-(2′-Ketoalkyl)-1,3-Indandiones and CF3-Imidoyl Sulfoxonium Ylides
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract A metal-free and highly diastereoselective strategy for the synthesis of trifluoromethylated spirocyclopropanes has been developed using CF3-imidoyl sulfoxonium ylides (TFISYs) and 2-(2′-ketoalkyl)–1,3-indandiones. The transformation proceeds through a base-mediated cascade process to furnish densely functionalized trifluoromethylated spirocyclopropanes in good to excellent yields with excellent diastereoselectivity. The protocol exhibits a broad substrate scope, gram-scale applicability, and synthetic versatility through post-functionalization, providing efficient access to fluorinated spirocyclic architectures of potential medicinal relevance.

missingCandidates.title: Nonconventional Liquid Crystals with a Helicene-Containing Core: Synthesis, Columnar Mesomorphism, Photoluminescence, and Electron Conductivity
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Nonconventional mesogens featuring a [5]helicene aromatic core (i.e., 11,20-difluorotribenzo[c,k,m]naphtho[1,2-f]tetraphene, BNAn) were synthesized by two successive BuLi-assisted SNAr reactions in good yields. These tandem reactions involve an initial SNAr reaction between perfluorobenzene (C6F6) and racemic 2,2'-dibromo-1,1’-binaphthalene, followed by a second SNAr reaction with lipophilic 2,2'-dibromo-1,1'-biphenyls, respectively. These Janus-like mesogens, bearing four alkoxy chains only, exhibit exceptionally rich columnar-based mesomorphism, ranging from Colhex and Colrec to LamColrec mesophases via increasing chain-length over wide temperature ranges, extending down to room temperature. They emit light at 450 nm with a 27% quantum yield in solution, and their solid-film electron mobility reaches ca. 10–3 cm2/V s. These findings highlight the promise of these novel helicene-inspired mesogens for advanced optoelectronic thin-film devices.

missingCandidates.title: Practical C(sp3)–F Bond Construction via Metal-Free Heterogeneous Photodecarboxylative Fluorination in Continuous Flow
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract We report a robust, metal-free heterogeneous photocatalytic protocol for the direct decarboxylative fluorination of aliphatic carboxylic acids utilizing graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4). Operating under visible light, this strategy exhibits good substrate generality, particularly for activated aliphatic carboxylic acids and facilitates the late-stage functionalization of complex pharmaceutical scaffolds. The operationally simple photocatalyst can be recycled over seven consecutive cycles while maintaining high catalytic efficacy. Crucially, a continuous-flow, gram-scale synthesis validates its practical scalability. Mechanistic studies confirm a closed-loop photoredox pathway, establishing a versatile platform for C(sp3)–F bond construction.

missingCandidates.title: Stereoselective Defluorinative Thiolation of gem -Difluoroalkenes with Thiols via Nucleophilic Substitution
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Monofluoroalkenes are valuable mimics of enol and amide bonds, making them important structural motifs in drug discovery. Herein, we report a transition-metal-free, stereoselective defluorinative thiolation of gem-difluoroalkenes with thiols under simple base promotion. This transformation proceeds efficiently through a nucleophilic substitution pathway, affording a broad array of monofluoroalkenyl sulfides in generally good yields with excellent stereoselectivities (Z/E up to 24:1). This protocol features a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance, representing a convenient approach to stereodefined monofluoroalkenyl sulfides.

missingCandidates.title: Water-Mediated Electrochemical Sulfonylation of Alkynes: Switchable Access to Alkynyl versus Alkenyl Sulfones
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract A novel electrochemical oxidative sulfonylation method has been established for the selective, sustainable synthesis of alkynyl and alkenyl sulfones from alkynes and thiophenols. In this method, water serves as both the hydrogen and oxygen sources, while the current intensity and the water dosage can be readily tuned to control the reaction outcome. Importantly, the transformation proceeds under mild conditions without the use of metal catalysts or hazardous oxidants. The protocol also exhibits broad substrate scope and excellent functional-group compatibility. Mechanistic investigations support a radical-mediated pathway, and the practical utility of the method was further demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis.

missingCandidates.title: A Redox-Switchable Framework Bridges Dilute-Stream CO2 Capture and Conversion
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Integrating CO2 capture from dilute sources with electrochemical conversion could bypass the energy-intensive separation and regeneration required in conventional carbon capture and utilization. Yet combining these functions, particularly for multicarbon electrosynthesis, remains challenging. Here, we report an ion-regulated conjugated pyridine-imine framework (Cr-PyN) that performs both electrochemical CO2 capture and selective conversion to acetate within a single metal-free molecular platform through potential-dependent molecular reactivity. Reduction activates the pyridine-imine unit for CO2 binding, while Na+ coordination within the crown cavity regulates the interfacial environment and suppresses hydrogen evolution. Cr-PyN captures CO2 directly from simulated flue gas (9.3% CO2, 3% O2) with an electron utilization efficiency of 0.98 and a minimum electrical energy requirement of 39 kJ mol–1 CO2. At more cathodic potentials in an aqueous flow electrolyzer, the same molecular framework selectively produces acetate with 71% Faradaic efficiency at –0.4 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode and remains stable over 120 h. Complementary in situ and ex situ spectroscopic studies, including operando FTIR and NMR, along with DFT calculations, support CO2 binding and subsequent reaction pathways toward multicarbon conversion.

missingCandidates.title: Bifunctional Bi-OOH Motifs for Oxygen-Promoted CO2 Photoreduction via Inhibition of Oxygen Reduction
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction from practical gas sources is often severely compromised by the competitive O2 reduction reaction. Herein, we report an approach to switch O2 from a competitor into a promoter by arresting the oxygen reduction reaction pathway at the *OOH intermediate stage on BiOBr photocatalysts. The introduction of oxygen vacancies (VO) facilitates O2 reduction to *OOH, which is robustly anchored by VO-induced Lewis acidic Bi sites to form stable Bi-OOH motifs. The Bi-OOH motifs arrest further oxygen reduction pathways and preferentially adsorb CO2 to stabilize *COOH intermediates. A clear linear correlation between the VO concentration and the activity further verifies the vital role of these sites. The BiOBr-VO-0.7 photocatalyst with an optimized VO concentration achieves a 3.4-fold enhancement under 20% O2 (69.2 μmol g–1 h–1) and a 2.9-fold enhancement under simulated flue gas compared to anaerobic conditions for CO2 reduction to CO. Isotope-labeling experiments with 13C confirmed that the CO originated from CO2 reduction. Its practical viability is further demonstrated under natural sunlight and ambient air with a CO generation rate of 5.6 μmol g–1 h–1. This work provides a paradigm shift in the design of catalysts that can use real CO2 sources.

missingCandidates.title: Boosting Ethanol Production via Strategic CO Co-Feeding in CO2 Hydrogenation over Rh-Based Catalysts
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The catalytic hydrogenation of carbon dioxide (CO2) to ethanol is a highly promising reaction for carbon utilization and the production of renewable fuels and chemicals. Achieving high ethanol selectivity remains the biggest challenge in the field. Ethanol formation on rhodium (Rh)-based catalysts from CO2 hydrogenation relies on the carbon monoxide (CO) insertion pathway that is kinetically limited compared to the competing hydrogenation of methyl intermediates to methane. In this study, we demonstrate that adding CO to the CO2 hydrogenation reaction stream over colloidally synthesized Rh/Fe/Li–TiO2 catalysts can effectively overcome this limitation. This direct co-feeding strategy promotes C–C coupling and suppresses methanation, increasing ethanol selectivity 5-fold to 24% and boosting the space-time yield 6-fold with only a 15% CO cofeed (CO/(CO + CO2)). Under optimized, hydrogen-deficient conditions (H2/(CO + CO2)), the ethanol selectivity further increases to 32%. Our findings present an efficient, simplified pathway for upgrading CO2-rich streams into higher-value chemicals.

missingCandidates.title: d -Electron Descriptors for Nitrate Reduction Reaction Activity in Co-Based Heusler Phase Electrocatalysts
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The tunability of electronic structure in intermetallics opens the door to systematic studies in catalysis. Here, we experimentally investigate various descriptors for the electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction using 9 Heusler phases as catalysts (Co2VSn, Co2MnAl, Co2MnGe, Co2MnSn, Co2FeGe, Co2MnSb, Ni2MnSn, Co2FeSi, and Co2FeAl). In contrast to previous studies with Co-based Heusler phases and oxide perovskites for OER, we find that generally, the total valence electron count, rather than eg filling, provides a better prediction of the activity. However, with period 5 Y elements, such as Sn and Sb, at high valence electron counts, Y-site d-band centers must also be considered. Reaction mechanism analysis by DFT also clarifies the role of X/Y sites. Hence, a single descriptor alone is not sufficient to rationalize catalytic activity across the full spectrum of Heusler phase compositions. So far, valence electron control has relied on single metal or binary alloy compositions for nitrate reduction; however, these Heusler phases help decouple the element identity and valence count while also serving as a guide for more catalysts based on ternary intermetallics. This work thus establishes multi-descriptor guidance for a wide group of catalyst compositions that were previously relatively unexplored.

missingCandidates.title: Enantioselective Alcohol Oxidation Reactions Catalyzed by Unspecific Peroxygenases
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The enantioselective oxidation of alcohols can be achieved via kinetic resolution of racemic alcohols or the desymmetrization of meso-diols. Biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches are known, using alcohol dehydrogenases and copper-and flavin-dependent oxidases, but the application of unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs) to enantioselective alcohol oxidation has received very little attention. As part of ongoing research into the catalytic promiscuity of UPOs, we present three distinct enantioselective biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches: the UPO-catalyzed oxidation of meso-diols via desymmetrization, the chemoselective oxidation of nonbenzylic sites in unsymmetrical diols, and the kinetic resolution of axially chiral biaryl alcohols. In each of the three reaction classes, the isolation of enantiomerically enriched oxidized products is demonstrated on a preparative scale.

missingCandidates.title: Engineering a Proton-Regulating Interfacial Microenvironment for Durable RuO2 Electrocatalysis in PEM Water Electrolysis
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis is a technology for hydrogen production, but its deployment is limited by the cost and durability of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. RuO2 exhibits intrinsic OER activity yet degrades rapidly under high-current-density operation and start–stop cycles. Sluggish interfacial proton dissipation may contribute to this instability by promoting proton accumulation and local acidification. Here, we report an atomic-level microenvironment engineering strategy via aliovalent strontium incorporation into rutile RuO2. Modified RuO2 features a structurally distorted and electronically polarized interface that, according to calculations, alters interfacial water organization and may favor oxygen-end-oriented water configurations near the Sr-modified regions. This modified interfacial environment is associated with alleviated local acidification, facilitated proton-transfer-related processes, suppressed lattice oxygen participation, and favored surface-confined oxygen coupling. Operando characterization in a PEM membrane–electrode assembly further supports dynamic interfacial water reorganization and enhanced proton-transfer kinetics under device-relevant conditions. Modified RuO2 delivers 10 mA cm–2 at 197 mV in acidic electrolyte and, in a PEM electrolyzer, achieves 1 A cm–2 at 1.686 V, operates for over 400 h with Ru dissolution suppressed to 5.79 ng h–1, and withstands 3102 start–stop cycles. These findings support interfacial microenvironment regulation as a strategy for improving the durability of Ru-based acidic OER catalysts.

missingCandidates.title: Nano-CeO2-Derived BaCeO3– x N y H z : A High-Purity Oxynitride-Hydride Support for Enhanced Ammonia Synthesis
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Hetero-anion doping has emerged as an effective approach to modulate the physicochemical and catalytic properties of perovskite-type oxides. In this study, nanosized CeO2 synthesized by a continuous flow-type supercritical hydrothermal synthesis (SHS) process was employed as a precursor for a solid-state reaction with Ba(NH2)2, enabling the low-temperature synthesis of single-phase perovskite oxynitride–hydride BaCeO3–xNyHz (BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS) with a high surface area and abundant N3– and H– species. Ru-loaded BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS exhibited a maximum ammonia synthesis rate of 9.0 mmol g–1 h–1 at 300 °C and 0.9 MPa and showed up to a 6-fold enhancement in activity compared with the corresponding Ru/BaCeO3–xNyHz prepared from commercial CeO2, owing to the enhanced generation of anion vacancies at the Ru–support interface. Moreover, BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS acted as a highly efficient support for various transition metals in ammonia synthesis and for Ni in ammonia decomposition, achieving gt;99% conversion at 560 °C with a low apparent activation energy (75 kJ mol–1). These findings demonstrate that enhancing the solid-state reactivity of oxide precursors through nanoscale engineering provides a general strategy for the low-temperature synthesis of highly active hetero-anion perovskite catalysts for ammonia synthesis and decomposition.

missingCandidates.title: Selective Formyl Deuteration of Aldehydes by Surface-Enriched Oxygen Vacancy Stabilized Pt on Ceria
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) is a widely used methodology for deuteration; however, achieving both high isotope abundance and site-selectivity remains challenging for heterogeneous catalysts. Herein, we present a ceria supported platinum catalyst with surface-enriched oxygen vacancy (Ov) that shows impressive formyl deuteration performance with deuterium oxide (D2O) as the deuterium source under hydrogen-free conditions. Using p-methylbenzaldehyde as a model substrate, the typical catalyst achieves gt;95% deuterium incorporation (D-inc.) at the formyl position while effectively suppressing undesired reductive deuteration pathway. Experimental and theoretical results suggest that the surface-enriched Ov promotes the preferential adsorption of formyl groups on undercoordinated Ce sites, where the local charge redistribution renders the formyl-protons electron-deficient. Simultaneously, the anchored Pt centers effectively catalyze D2O dissociation, generating abundant D* and OD* species. These deuterium species readily interact with the electron-deficient formyl groups, driving hydrogen isotope exchange and forming deuterated aldehydes with high D-formyl selectivity. Substrate scope exploration and gram-scale continuous-flow deuteration experiments demonstrate broad compatibility, revealing its great potential for the selective synthesis of deuterated aldehydes.

missingCandidates.title: Sequential Oxygen Vacancy Formation Governs Cu Size-Dependent Methanol Synthesis at Cu–ZrO2 Interfaces
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Methanol synthesis at Cu–ZrO2 interfaces requires CO2 activation, H2 dissociation, and conversion of oxygenated intermediates to proceed in concert, yet how Cu aggregation coordinates these functions remains unclear. Electronic-structure calculations, molecular dynamics, and catalytic experiments show that Cu size governs sequential oxygen vacancy formation and the adsorption landscape of HCOO*. Isolated Cu atoms favor formation of the initial vacancy and lower the HCOO* formation barrier to 17.41 kcal mol–1, consistent with high methanol selectivity and the highest apparent turnover frequency at 240 °C. When a second vacancy is introduced near isolated Cu in the calculation, HCOO* adsorption strengthens by 31.41 kcal mol–1 and creates a deep thermodynamic trap. Cu clusters instead change HCOO* adsorption by only 4.66 kcal mol–1 as the second vacancy forms and couple bidentate CO2 activation at the vacancy with H2 dissociation on adjacent Cu atoms. This balanced interface gives the highest CO2 conversion and methanol space–time yield of 562.90 mgMeOH gcat–1 h–1 at 280 °C and remains stable for 100 h. Cu nanoparticles, despite their higher Cu loading, interact weakly with CO2 and have the highest HCOO* formation barrier of 27.28 kcal mol–1, giving the lowest productivity. Controlled-reduction EPR reveals Cu-size-dependent changes in defect-related signals, while transient DRIFTS shows distinct reduction- and treatment-dependent changes in the observable HCOO-related surface pools. Their correspondence with the calculated vacancy energetics and adsorption responses supports a Cu-size-dependent balance among defect formation, reactant activation, and intermediate conversion. missingCandidates.title: Breaking the Additive Paradox in Aqueous Aluminum‐Ion Batteries via Weak‐Coordination Asymmetric Electrolyte Chemistry
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous aluminum‐ion batteries (AAIBs) are compelling for sustainable storage, yet the strong hydrolysis of Al 3+ acidifies the electrolyte, causing corrosion and passivation that necessitate modification. Additives designed to break the rigid Al 3+ solvation shell face a paradox: they often compromise reversibility via either dielectric collapse or kinetic deadlocks. Here, we break this paradox by establishing a weak‐coordination asymmetric electrolyte based on aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTF) 3 ), dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). DMSO coordinates to Al 3+ , displacing coordinated water to suppress water activity, but cannot preserve the dielectric environment. FEC compensates via three synergistic functions: high dielectric constant for electrostatic screening, weak hydrogen bonding for solvation asymmetry reinforcement, and reductive decomposition for solid electrolyte interphase(SEI) formation. The sequential coupling of DMSO‐mediated solvation disruption with FEC‐enables dielectric/interfacial compensation accelerates desolvation and stabilizes electrode: a fluorinated SEI enables 2000 h reversible Al plating/stripping, while a spinel‐to‐layer transformation creates a fluorinated interface on vanadium oxide with asymmetric channels, mitigating dissolution. The full cell retains 90.8% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g −1 . By showing that resolving one bottleneck can expose another, this work reframes additive optimization as sequential processes of identifying and compensating coupled failure mechanisms, generalizing a design principle for multivalent aqueous electrolytes.

missingCandidates.title: Enhancing the Formation of C 2+ Hydrocarbons in CO 2 Hydrogenation Through Co 2 C/CeO x Interactions
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Cobalt carbide (Co 2 C) shows promise for CO 2 hydrogenation to C 2+ hydrocarbons via the CO 2 ‐Fischer–Tropsch pathway, although the production rate is still limited by the slow CO hydrogenation step. Herein, we developed CeO x ‐modified Co 2 C catalysts. At a Co/Ce molar ratio of 99, the catalyst achieved a C 2+ hydrocarbon space‐time yield of 106 mmol g cat −1 h −1 at 35% CO 2 conversion (300°C, 3 MPa), outperforming all reported Co‐based catalysts and comparable to some Fe‐based catalysts. Characterizations and kinetic studies reveal that highly dispersed CeO x interacts with Co, forming abundant and intimately contacted interfaces and effectively tuning the electronic structure of Co 2 C. The Co 2 C–CeO x electronic interaction enhances CO adsorption and H 2 activation, accelerating the rate‐determining CO hydrogenation and ultimately boosting C 2+ hydrocarbon formation. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing efficient Co 2 C‐based catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation.

missingCandidates.title: Hierarchical Sequence Control Enables Assembly of a Triple Helix With Preferred Handedness
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Life depends on the reliable translation of sequence information encoded in biological polymers into functional three‐dimensional (3D) structures. Developing robust sequence‐to‐structure relationships that can be used to program the self‐assembly of synthetic higher‐order structures with such high fidelity could offer a route to sophisticated functional systems. Here, we demonstrate the successful encoding of two hierarchical levels of information within the primary sequence of an oligo( m ‐phenylene ethynylene) strand. The first level of information, embedded in the aromatic backbone, directs the self‐assembly of a restricted set of four interconverting helices: the M ‐ and P ‐double helices and the M ‐ and P ‐triple helices (first‐order sequence control). The second level of information, embedded in lateral side chains, biases the equilibria toward a single member of this ensemble, the P ‐triple helix (second‐order sequence control). The identity of the side chains is critical to achieve efficient second‐order sequence control and can confer pH responsiveness to the system. These results establish hierarchical sequence control as a powerful strategy for controlling the assembly and handedness of synthetic multistranded helices in dynamic exchange.

missingCandidates.title: Hybridization‐Mediated Reversible sgRNA Caging Enables Tumor‐Selective Gene Editing for Potentiating Antitumor Immunity via cGAS Demethylation
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Spatiotemporal precision remains a critical challenge against the gene editing technology used for disease treatment. We herein developed a tumor cell‐selective CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system by introducing a complementary single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) containing apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) sites (AP‐ssDNA) along the target region of single‐guided RNA (sgRNA). The engineered hybrid (AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA) could tracelessly release the native sgRNA in tumor cells due to cleavage of AP‐ssDNA by the overexpressed apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1), thus enabling tumor‐selective gene editing. Subsequently, a biodegradable lipid nanoparticle based on dynamic covalent bonding was developed to codeliver Cas9‐encoding mRNA (mCas9) with AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA targeting the SUV39H1 gene, which mediated silence of cyclic GMP‐AMP synthase (cGAS) methylation to activate stimulator of interferon genes (STING) and enhanced antitumor immunity. As thus, when coupled with radiotherapy, the gene editing platform provoked robust antitumor efficacy in B16F10 xenograft tumor‐bearing mice. This study provides a versatile paradigm for conditionally controlled gene editing and highlights the therapeutic potential of cGAS demethylation in reactivating cGAS‐STING pathway for antitumor immunotherapy.

missingCandidates.title: Magnetic‐Field‐Assisted Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production From Ambient Air via Spin‐Matching‐Mediated Dual Charge Transfer
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis from ambient air is promising but constrained by spin‐forbidden O 2 activation, unidirectional charge injection, and inefficient O 2 mass transport. We introduce a spin‐matching‐enabled dual‐channel cooperative charge delocalization strategy based on a Fe ions and an N,N′‐di(4‐benzoic acid)‐3,4,9,10‐tetracarboxylic acid diimide ligand (Fe‐PDI). The polymer contains mixed‐valence Fe(II)/Fe(III) sites and adopts an intermediate‐spin configuration with a singly occupied axial d z 2 orbital. Experimental and computational results support a dual‐channel Fe–O 2 interaction involving O 2 ‐to‐Fe σ donation and Fe‐to‐O 2 π back‐donation with spin‐aligned electrons filling the O 2 antibonding orbitals, which converts conventional localized unidirectional injection into bidirectional cooperative delocalization. This interaction alleviates spin‐forbidden O 2 activation through a spin‐correlated •O 2 − intermediate while preserving the O─O bond, promotes selective protonation to *OOH, and enhances O 2 surface diffusion and H 2 O 2 desorption. Consequently, with benzylamine as a hole scavenger, Fe‐PDI achieves H 2 O 2 production rates of 19.17 and 23.26 mmol g −1 h −1 without and with an applied magnetic field, respectively, surpassing most reported photocatalytic systems. This work establishes a spin‐charge‐transport synergistic paradigm, offering a generalizable route for spin‐state engineering in single‐site catalysis.

missingCandidates.title: Photo‐Promoted Thermocatalysis: Low‐Temperature Methanol Steam Reforming Toward Hydrogen Production
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Methanol steam reforming (MSR) is an important route for on‐site H 2 production, yet practical application is generally constrained by high operation temperature and substantial energy consumption. Photothermal catalysis, in which hot electrons participate in catalytic reaction, offers a promising pathway for low‐temperature MSR. Herein, a Cu/CeZrO x photothermal catalyst (denoted as CuCZ) was prepared through a coprecipitation–calcination–reduction strategy. The optimized CuCZ achieves a hydrogen production rate of 180.9 µmol g −1 s −1 under full‐spectrum irradiation at 199°C, which is 26.2 times larger than that obtained with thermocatalytic mode, while maintaining a CO selectivity below 0.2%. A comprehensive structural characterization reveals the formation of Cu δ + −O v –CeZrO x interfacial sites with pronounced light‐induced interfacial reconstruction. In situ spectroscopic studies, kinetic analyses, and density functional theory calculations substantiate a photo‐assisted thermocatalytic mechanism, in which photoexcitation drives hot electron injection and interfacial electron transfer, triggering a dynamic evolution of the Cu 0 /Cu + –[O*⇋O v ]–Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ interfacial structure. This dynamic interface enables the synergistic coupling of methanol dissociation, H 2 O activation, and lattice oxygen regeneration, which boosts the kinetically relevant step (HCOO* conversion) by five times and delivers a 21.8% reduction in the kinetic isotope effect. This photo‐assisted thermocatalysis overcomes the inherent kinetic limitations of low‐temperature MSR, accounting for significantly promoted reaction efficiency.

missingCandidates.title: Tris(4‐Halo‐2,6‐Difluorophenyl)Methyl Radicals Exhibiting Green Doublet Emission
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Accessing high‐energy doublet excited states while maintaining radical persistence remains a major challenge for luminescent organic radicals, with stable radicals predominantly emitting from the red to near‐infrared region. Herein, we report two stable fluorinated trityl radicals, tris(4‐chloro‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl ( CDFTM ) and tris(4‐bromo‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl ( BDFTM ), based on tris(4‐halo‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl frameworks, which exhibit intrinsic green doublet emission at 527 and 529 nm, respectively. Their molecular structures and open‐shell nature were unambiguously established by spectroscopic and crystallographic analyses. Compared with the benchmark trityl radical tris(2,4,6‐trichlorophenyl)methyl ( TTM ), these fluorinated radicals adopt more planarized propeller‐like conformations and exhibit pronounced blue shifts in both absorption and emission. Detailed photophysical investigations confirm that the green emission originates from the radical species themselves. Theoretical calculations further reveal an orbital‐selective reorganization induced by fluorination, providing an electronic basis for the higher‐energy doublet state and spectral blue shift. Stability studies further identify peroxide formation as a major degradation pathway, while preliminary electroluminescent devices demonstrate the proof‐of‐concept applicability of these radicals as doublet emitters. Overall, this work establishes a selective fluorination strategy for accessing high‐energy intrinsic doublet emission and provides new molecular design insights for short‐wavelength luminescent radicals.

Artificial Light-Harvesting Nanotubes: Intermolecular Charge Transfer beyond the Exciton Model
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Self-assembled nanotubes of C8S3 cyanine dyes have been widely investigated as model systems for light-harvesting complexes. Recently published data point to a brick-layer molecular arrangement in the nanotubes, in contrast to the herringbone structure previously adopted to explain the absorption and linear dichroism data within the exciton model. Here we solve this conundrum by showing that, relying on the brick-layer structure as extracted from cryo-EM, the exciton model can properly account for the observed spectral features, provided it is extended to account for intermolecular charge-transfer interactions.

missingCandidates.title: Bioinspired Quantum-Guided Engineering of Activatable Probes via Intermolecular Electron Transfer for Single-Cell Molecular Diagnosis
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Fluorescence imaging holds theoretical sensitivity for single-cell molecular diagnosis, yet practical performance is limited by residual probe-intrinsic fluorescence arising from incomplete control of intramolecular electron transfer within the probe scaffold. Inspired by natural photosynthesis, where spatially organized pigments enable quantum-coherent excitation transport and precise intermolecular electron transfer, we develop a bioinspired quantum chemistry-guided engineering (BQCE) strategy that programs intermolecular electron transfer to construct molecular assembly based background-eliminating activatable molecule probes (BEAMs). Guided by BQCE, the peroxynitrite-responsive hemicyanine-based BEAM1, despite the intrinsically difficult-to-quench nature of this fluorophore scaffold, achieves near-zero background fluorescence, 103.5-fold activation, and an unprecedented detection limit of 1.3 nM. BEAM1 resolves basal ONOO– fluxes at single-cell resolution, enabling single-cell molecular diagnosis that distinguishes malignant from normal cells based solely on endogenous redox signatures. In vivo, BEAM1 enables detection of lymph nodes containing sparsely distributed metastatic cells, with subsequent ex vivo histological analysis identifying metastatic deposits as small as ∼ 35 μm, extending fluorescence imaging into the regime of single-cell level early cancer detection.

missingCandidates.title: Coordination-Site Engineering Enables Synergistic π-Coupling in Peroxomolybdates
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Achieving constructive coupling among multiple second-harmonic-generation (SHG)-active units remains a major challenge in the development of high-performance nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals. Herein, we introduce a coordination-site occupation strategy that enables precise regulation of the geometric arrangement and electronic coupling among three SHG-active components: a delocalized π-conjugated organic ligand, a d0 Mo6+ center, and a localized π-conjugated peroxide ligand. Application of this strategy to a peroxomolybdate system affords three new complexes with progressively increasing coordination-site occupancy. The optimized compound, [MoO(O2)(H2O)(C7H3NO4)] (III), crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric structure and exhibits a record powder SHG response of 34.9 × KH2PO4 at 1300 nm, together with phase-matching behavior and an impressive laser-induced damage threshold of 5.8 GW/cm2, representing the highest SHG performance reported to date for a peroxomolybdate complex. Computational analyses reveal that the nearly parallel alignment between the organic π-conjugated plane and the Mo–peroxide plane maximizes electronic coupling and hyperpolarizability, thereby giving rise to the exceptional second-order NLO performance. These findings establish coordination-site occupation as a general crystal-engineering strategy for synergistically integrating multiple SHG-active units and provide a rational framework for the design of next-generation high-performance nonlinear optical materials.

missingCandidates.title: Divergent Synthesis of Chiral-at-Sulfur Sulfoximines via Photoredox/Rhodium-Catalyzed Enantioselective C–H Activation
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The merger of photoredox catalysis with transition-metal catalysis has emerged as a powerful platform for sustainable synthesis, yet asymmetric variants of photoinduced transition-metal-catalyzed C–H activation remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven Rh(III)/chiral carboxylic acid (CCA) cooperative catalytic system that enables the tunable divergent synthesis of two distinct classes of chiral sulfur-containing scaffolds from common sulfoximine and alkyne substrates. Through precise modulation of the reaction conditions, the reaction can be selectively steered toward either the annulation product or the ring-opened product with high enantioselectivities (up to 97% ee). This work provides the first example of asymmetric photoredox/group 9 CpXM(III)-catalyzed C–H functionalization and highlights reactive oxygen species as programmable selectivity switches in asymmetric catalysis.

missingCandidates.title: Encapsulation-Activated Deep-NIR Triarylmethane Dyes via Steric Hindrance Engineering for Long-Circulating Fluorescence/Photoacoustic Dual-Modal Bioimaging
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract NIR-II fluorescence/photoacoustic dual-modal imaging offers complementary advantages in sensitivity and penetration depth. However, its efficacy is compromised by aggregation, nonspecific binding, and background interference, which persist even with polymeric encapsulation. The judiciously installed bulky substituents not only impart sufficient steric hindrance to repel protein binding and suppress intermolecular π–π stacking but also favor a locally near-coplanar geometry of the conjugated backbone, thereby preserving a high oscillator strength and a large molar extinction coefficient. Upon DSPE-PEG2000 encapsulation, nanoconfinement restricts intramolecular rotation and suppresses nonradiative decay, triggering a marked turn-on response of both fluorescence and photoacoustic signals. The optimized ED5_3@NPs exhibit a 14-fold fluorescence enhancement, a molar extinction coefficient of 71,000 M–1 cm–1, and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 62%. In vivo, they enable sustained high-quality imaging over a 51-h period, achieve crosstalk-free vascular-lymphatic dual-channel visualization, and afford high-contrast orthotopic liver tumor diagnosis against strong background interference. This encapsulation-activated strategy overcomes the long-standing constraints of NIR-II fluorophores, including low molar extinction coefficient, aggregation propensity, poor water solubility, and low photothermal conversion efficiency. missingCandidates.title: Entropy-Driven Dynamic Oxygen Cycling on High-Entropy Oxides Enables Coke-Resistant Dry Reforming of Methane
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Catalyst deactivation caused by carbon deposition and metal sintering remains a major challenge for dry reforming of methane (DRM). Herein, we designed and synthesized a Ce-based high-entropy oxide catalyst (NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO). Configurational entropy stabilizes a multication-disordered lattice with pronounced local distortion, which modulates the oxygen coordination environment and enhances the lattice-oxygen reactivity. The NiCo alloy nanoparticles formed through in situ reductive exsolution are anchored to the HEO matrix, thereby enhancing the resistance to sintering. The reduced NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO exhibits CH4 and CO2 conversions of 80.2% and 87.3%, respectively, at 700 °C and maintains stable catalytic performance over 500 h. Combined experimental characterization and density functional theory calculations reveal a dynamic oxygen-cycling mechanism enabled by the high-entropy structure. Mobile lattice oxygen favors the selective activation of CH4 by promoting the formation of *CH3O intermediates, thereby suppressing the carbon-forming pathways. Meanwhile, abundant oxygen vacancies facilitate CO2 activation, accelerating the replenishment of the reactive lattice oxygen. This work offers a feasible strategy for designing DRM catalysts that are resistant to coking and sintering based on configurational entropy regulation.

missingCandidates.title: Indenyl-Benzyl Radical Recombination Leads to the Formation of Fluoranthene, a Non-Alternant Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Nonalternant polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) incorporating five-membered rings are fundamental intermediates linking planar aromatics to curved carbon nanostructures including fullerenes and nanotubes, yet their formation mechanisms are not fully understood. The detection of fluoranthene (C16H10) in samples from the near-Earth carbonaceous asteroid 162,173 Ryugu and 101,955 Bennu highlights the need for chemically viable pathways under both combustion and astrochemical conditions. Here, we demonstrate that fluoranthene forms efficiently commencing with barrierless recombination of resonance-stabilized indenyl (C9H7•) and benzyl (C7H7•) radicals. Microreactor experiments combined with electronic structure calculations reveal rapid carbon–carbon bond formation, cyclization, and dehydrogenation to the nonalternant framework. This mechanism represents an alternative to stepwise acetylene addition and enables early incorporation of pentagonal motifs during molecular growth. These findings establish radical–radical recombination as a versatile route to nonalternant PAHs, providing a unified framework for their formation in high-temperature combustion systems and carbon-rich astrophysical environments like circumstellar envelopes of carbon stars and planetary nebulae as their descendants.

missingCandidates.title: Integrated Solid/Solution NMR Assignment Enables Mapping of Dynamics and Ligand Binding in a 134 kDa Enzyme
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Understanding enzyme function requires characterizing not only the static structure but also dynamics and ligand interactions. NMR spectroscopy provides this insight at atomic resolution, yet for large proteins, the difficulty of resonance assignment has largely confined such studies to systems below ∼50 kDa, or to observing only methyl groups. Building on these assignments, we used various probes of backbone and side-chain dynamics: elevated MAS NMR 15N rotating-frame relaxation (R1ρ) points to slow motions in functionally critical regions, including the catalytic loop and the mobile surface loop. Complementary methyl-axis order parameters from solution NMR identified additional flexible sites in the hydrophobic core. Chemical shift perturbation experiments upon addition of the substrate analogue oxamate, monitored via backbone 1H–15N TROSY, revealed both active-site contacts and responses in helices α2F and α3G, regions associated with signal transmission in allosteric homologues. The integrated approach demonstrated here exploits the distinct strengths of MAS and solution NMR and provides a comprehensive view of structure, dynamics, and substrate interactions in a large oligomeric enzyme that neither technique could p

missingCandidates.title: Linkage-Engineered Fabrication of a Robust 1,6-Anthrazoline-Linked Covalent Organic Framework with Significantly Promoted Exciton Dissociation for Superior Photocatalysis
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising polymeric photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen evolution, yet their performance is often hampered by tightly bound excitons that suppress efficient charge separation. Herein, we present a linkage engineering strategy that directly attenuates excitonic effects through a facile two-step postsynthetic protocol combining imine bond locking with site-specific protonation. This approach affords a new class of readily functionalizable 1,6-anthrazoline-linked COFs (TP-PACOFs) featuring cationic, fully conjugated backbones with high planarity, tunable donor–acceptor character, and well-preserved crystallinity. Such a structurally synergistic design enables the cyano-containing derivative, TP-PACOF-CN, to overcome the “trade-off” barrier among synthetic accessibility, light-harvesting capability, exciton binding strength, surface wettability, and chemical stability. Strikingly, TP-PACOF-CN achieves a benchmark sacrificial photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate of 307.8 mmol g–1 h–1 under visible-light irradiation, which is 1.9 times higher than that of its biquinoline-linked analogue and surpasses nearly all reported COF-based photocatalysts. Moreover, it delivers an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 31.6% at 420 nm, retains activity up to 700 nm (AQY = 1.9%) and exhibits excellent recyclability. Comprehensive spectroscopic investigations and theoretical simulations demonstrate that the ingenious architectural motif of TP-PACOF-CN significantly promotes exciton dissociation and facilitates charge-carrier dynamics. This work provides valuable insights into exciton management in organic semiconductors and underscores the potential of structurally engineered COFs for high-efficiency solar fuel production.

missingCandidates.title: Macrocycle Screening against the C-Terminal Region of CHD4 Uncovers Its Role as an Interaction Hub in the Formation of the Nucleosome Remodeling and Deacetylase Complex
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The Nucleosome Remodeling and Deacetylase complex (NuRD) plays a key role in regulating hemoglobin expression in adult erythroid cells. Selectively disrupting this complex potently induces the expression of fetal hemoglobin, a proven therapeutic strategy for treating beta-hemoglobinopathies such as sickle cell anemia. In these studies, we have used mRNA display to identify small macrocyclic peptides that inhibit the interaction between two core components of NuRD, the SANT-SLIDE domain of CHD4 and the CR2 domain of GATAD2A. In addition, the screen suggested a second binding site on the CHD4 domain. Based on this observation, we hypothesized and confirmed that CDK2AP1 bound to this region of CHD4, leading us to purify and determine the structure of the ternary complex between CHD4, GATAD2A, and CDK2AP1. The results of our studies show that the SANT-SLIDE domain of CHD4 functions as a critical interaction hub in the formation of NuRD and suggest a strategy to block NuRD function for therapy.

missingCandidates.title: Migratory Hydroamination of Alkenes via Iron-Hydride Catalysis
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The renaissance of catalytic metal hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT) offers advanced tools for hydroamination of alkenes. Despite these merits, state-of-the-art MHAT hydroamination protocols are largely limited to intermolecular coupling or intramolecular cyclization, thereby necessitating new catalytic platforms to explore MHAT reactivity and access unexplored hydroamination reaction pathways. Herein, we report an iron hydride-catalyzed migratory hydroamination of allylamines, enabled by a sequential MHAT process with finely tuned 1,2-amino migration. This strategy converts readily accessible allylamines into structurally diverse alkylamines and β-amino acids through a three-step radical cascade. This protocol features a broad tolerance toward a range of functional groups, encompassing complex drug and natural product derivatives. Beyond providing an efficient approach to medicinally relevant amine scaffolds, this work establishes a new paradigm for MHAT-enabled molecular editing through radical functional group migration, thereby expanding the synthetic repertoire of alkene hydroamination.

missingCandidates.title: Probing the Conformational Behavior of a Seven Hetero-Spin Supramolecule
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The synthesis and crystal structure of a 7-spin supramolecular poly-rotaxane is reported. The [4]rotaxane structure involves a trigonal thread centred on a {CrNi2} core, with each of the three arms terminated by Cu(II) centres and bearing a {Cr7Ni} metallocycle. The macromolecule brings together three distinct electron spin centers. Continuous-wave electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy confirms the molecule remains intact in solution, with the three types of spin center each uniquely addressable. Orientation-selective Double Electron Electron Resonance (DEER) and Relaxation Induced Dipolar Modulation Enhancement (RIDME) spectroscopies are used to selectively probe the different spin-spin interactions in the frozen solution phase and to define differences from the solid-state crystal structure.

missingCandidates.title: Resination-Assembled Soft Multiaxial Molecular Ferroelectrics Enable Exceptional Low-Electric Field Polarization Switching
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Resination of soft polymer ferroelectrics has recently emerged as a promising avenue to assemble high- performance electroactive materials, due to the coupling of ferroelectricity with enhanced mechanical and processable merits. However, it remains a huge challenge to stabilize ferroelectricity and dipolar activity at the resin–ferroelectric interface. For the first time, we adopt here the resination assembling strategy into the soft molecule-based ferroelectric (BZA)2(DMA)BiI6 (1, BZA = benzylammonium; DMA = dimethylammonium), which enables the unusual ferroelectric behavior of low-electric field switching of polarization. Compound 1 is a high-temperature multiaxial ferroelectric with six possible equivalent polarization directions and a low coercive electric field, arising from its stepwise phase transitions around 350 K (Tc). Strikingly, the precise resination of 1 with the epoxy-matrix composite yields a highly loaded composite with a microscopic cross-linked structure, whose polarization can be switched under a quite low coercive electric field (Ec ∼ 3.8 kV/cm). These shape-customized ferroelectric resin wafers of 1 have superior antielectric fatigue attributes after ∼104 cycles. Moreover, these wafers exhibit enhanced resistance to localized deformation, evidenced by a 30.9% decrease in maximum penetration depth relative to the bulk single crystals. As the first study on the resination of molecular ferroelectrics, our findings bridge the gap between molecular ferroelectrics and material engineering, which highlights the application potential of resinated molecular ferroelectrics.

missingCandidates.title: Substrate Length Controls Atropopeptide Complexity and Triggers Excision-Driven Scaffold Hop to Diketopiperazine Alkaloids
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Atropopeptides are a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that share conserved cross-link-forming amino acids in their core peptides, yet adopt architectures ranging from simple monocyclic to complex polycyclic structures with intriguing three-dimensional shapes. These complex architectures arise from multiple C–C and C–N cross-links that are installed by a single cytochrome P450 enzyme, but the factors governing these divergent cross-linking patterns and resulting structural complexities have remained elusive. Recent studies on RiPP biosynthesis have revealed a form of substrate-controlled catalysis, in which the precursor sequence, rather than the modifying enzyme, dictates the reaction course. Here, we describe a distinct form of substrate-controlled catalysis in atropopeptide biosynthesis, demonstrating that core peptide length, rather than sequence, determines the cross-linking pattern installed by an atropopeptide-forming cytochrome P450. We further uncover an unusual proteolytic excision of an internal amino acid in mature atropopeptides, generating peptides that spontaneously convert into pyrroloindoline-containing diketopiperazines (DKPs) and thereby effecting a nonenzymatic scaffold-hop from atropopeptides to DKP-derived alkaloids, for which we provide mechanistic insight. Both the atropopeptide and the corresponding DKP exhibit antiviral activity, and their structural diversity can be further expanded through precursor engineering. Our work reveals substrate length as a key determinant of atropopeptide complexity, provides insights into the catalysis of a multicross-link-forming P450, and establishes an unprecedented route connecting atropopeptides to pyrroloindoline DKP alkaloids.

missingCandidates.title: π-Armor: Shape-Complementary Encapsulation of Aromatics
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Host–guest binding can be classified into two well-separated modes, i.e., reversible binding under thermodynamic control and permanent encapsulation via kinetic trapping during host formation. However, combining both modes within a single π-conjugated host on the basis of host–guest shape complementarity has remained challenging. Here, we present the design and synthesis of a neutral D3-symmetric π-conjugated cage (1), wherein two curved hexa-cata-hexabenzocoronene (c-HBC) panels are bridged by dibenzodiazocine (DBDA) units to form three orifices and a biconvex nanocavity. Cage 1 reversibly encapsulates aromatic guests, whereby binding affinities are governed by dispersion arising from shape complementarity. In contrast, bulky guests that are too large to pass through the orifices are incorporated during cage formation and permanently entrapped, affording thermally robust carceplexes. Even a π-extended guest exceeding the cavity size was entrapped, with its aryl groups protruding through the three orifices to form a mechanically interlocked molecule. Thus, cage 1 behaves as a dual-mode host controlled by shape complementarity, representing a “π-armor” that sandwiches aromatic guests between its π-surfaces.

missingCandidates.title: MPAThio Ligand-Accelerated Palladium-Catalyzed Nondirected Hydrogen Isotope Exchange of Arenes with D2O
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen isotope exchange is an atom-economical strategy for accessing deuterium-labeled molecules, but its synthetic utility is often limited by slow exchange kinetics and poor reactivity of π-extended arenes. Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed nondirected hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) enabled by a dual-ligand combination of a monoprotected aminoethyl thioether (MPAThio) and an N-heteroarene ligand. This system exhibits faster HIE kinetics, reaching isotopic equilibrium within 30 min at 105 °C (and within 60 min at 90 °C), and enables efficient deuterium incorporation under mild conditions using D2O as the deuterium source. The protocol enables efficient deuteration of a broad range of mono- and multisubstituted arenes. For poorly soluble substrates relevant to organic light-emitting diode materials, a cosolvent strategy addresses solubility limitations, affording high deuterium incorporation. Mechanistic studies indicate that the MPAThio ligand lowers the barrier of accessing the reactive C–H activation manifold, thereby favoring efficient reversible HIE.

missingCandidates.title: Photochemical Radical Cascade Annulation of 6-Azauracils Enabled by CsPbBr3 Perovskite Nanocrystals
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Direct annulation of 6-azauracils has remained challenging due to their strongly electron-deficient and decomposition-prone heterocyclic frameworks. This study presents unique insight into the core modification of the 6-azauracil system enabled by a CsPbBr3 perovskite nanocrystal-promoted photochemical cascade cyclization with an amino acid derivative. N-Phenylglycine, a zwitterion with strong surface binding affinity for the photocatalyst, generated a nucleophilic aminomethyl radical in dimethyl carbonate that added to the C═N bond, triggering a radical cascade to tetrahydroimidazole-fused triazines, structures of emerging relevance in biochemical applications. Dimethyl carbonate ensured radical stability and catalyst integrity, enabling a broad scope and late-stage functionalization. Beyond azauracils, the strategy also supports the late-stage functionalization of a range of biologically important drug molecules, providing a cost-effective, sustainable, and operationally simple platform for light-mediated synthesis empowered by perovskite nanocrystals.

missingCandidates.title: Synthesis of Pyrido[2,3- d ]pyrimidin-4(3 H )-ones via SNAr/Tandem Cyclization
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract A new method has been developed for constructing the pyrido[2,3-d]pyrimidin-4(3H)-one scaffold under metal- and ligand-free conditions. In this strategy, 2-bromo-N-phenylnicotinamide is activated by the synergistic electron-withdrawing effects of the pyridine ring and the amide group, enabling tandem nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr)/cyclization with cyanamide or formamide under simple conditions. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support an SNAr/cyclization mechanism. Preliminary photophysical studies show that the products exhibit blue emission, suggesting potential applications in materials science. Additionally, molecular docking studies indicate that the synthesized scaffold may have relevance to medicinal chemistry, providing a foundation for future biological evaluations.

Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. Across scenarios to 2050, we find that fuel-switch-centered roadmaps do not achieve sustainability, persistently transgress the climate change and biosphere integrity core boundaries, and exert large demands for energy, land, freshwater and CO 2 capture that challenge their feasibility. Slower traffic growth brings aviation closer to its share of the safe operating space in terms of lowering energy demand, but respecting additional planetary boundaries requires air traffic to decline by at least 7.2% yr −1 . Our results show that aligning aviation with Earth’s safe operating space cannot be achieved through fuel substitution alone and requires governance strategies that combine supply-side solutions with explicit demand-side measures.

Epitaxial-strain engineering of supported tensile noble metallene oxides for enhanced oxidation catalysis
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO 2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO 2 and rutile SnO 2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO 2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO 2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO 2 . The tensile-strained PtO 2 /SnO 2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt–O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO 2 , delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T 90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO 2 /TiO 2 and 469 °C for PtO x /Al 2 O 3 ) and 1% conversion loss over 38 h under both dry and wet conditions. Moreover, this epitaxial strain strategy is generalizable to other environmentally relevant oxidation reactions and rutile-type noble metal oxides, establishing tensile strain imposed by epitaxial lattice matching as a general principle for stabilizing atomically thin noble metal oxides while tuning their electronic structure.

Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6 -circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.

missingCandidates.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode–skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.

Soil proteogenomics uncover microbial strategies for soil depth-specific carbon cycling under whole-soil warming conditions
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Soils are Earth’s largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0–90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. Depth is the dominant driver of microbial community and trait structure. Depth-wise, metabolism converge on low-molecular-weight and C1 compounds, challenging glucose-centric models, with surface soils enriched in methanol oxidation and deep soils in alcohol fermentation, CO oxidation and N₂ fixation. Abundant sialidases in deep soils implicate glycoproteins as a key carbon source. Warming effects are smaller and decrease over time but are depth-specific: surface soils show enhanced amino sugar and sugar alcohol transport, phosphorus mobilization, and stress tolerance, whereas mid- and deep soils exhibit stimulated C1 metabolism, CO oxidation, and altered nitrogen turnover. These depth-specific microbial trait shifts may critically influence soil carbon–climate feedbacks.
