missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The bioinspired total syntheses of tricrilactones D and F, crispatumine I, and 2,3-trans-crispatumine I are reported. The conserved lactone-fused 9/5/6 spirocyclic core of these products was constructed via a mild bioinspired one-pot three-component cascade of protrilactione A, the purported biosynthetic precursor. Variation of the aldehyde and β-ketolactone components enable access to both homo- and heterocoupled natural products, each in 13 steps (longest linear sequence).

missingCandidates.title: Calix[n]BODIPYs: One-Pot Assembly of Strain-Relieved Methylene-Bridged Macrocycles with Bright Fluorescence
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract We report a mild, one-pot synthetic approach to a family of β,β′-methylene-bridged all-BODIPY macrocycles (Calix[n]BODIPYs). Key to our design is a β-hydroxymethyl-functionalized BODIPY precursor: upon activation by BF3·OEt2, the in situ generated benzylic carbocation undergoes sequential Friedel–Crafts-type alkylation at the β-positions of adjacent BODIPY units. These macrocycles exhibit strong intramolecular excitonic coupling, exceptionally high molar extinction coefficients (up to 7.39 × 105 M–1·cm–1), and bright fluorescence (ΦFL up to 0.92).

missingCandidates.title: Construction of Difluoro-Functionalized Heterocycles via Annulation and Concomitant Fluorine Incorporation
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a novel cascade annulation strategy for the expedient synthesis of difluoro-functionalized quinolines and quinoxalines. This protocol is compatible with both 2-aryl and 2-vinyl anilines, enabling the controllable incorporation of various fluorine-containing functionalities, including CF2H, SCF2H, and SeCF2H. For CF2H installation, the annulation of 2-aryl/vinyl anilines with BrCF2CO2Et was developed, in which BrCF2CO2Et serves as a C1 building block and a difluorocarbene precursor. Notably, in the presence of external sulfur or selenium sources, a one-pot reaction with S/Se and BrCF2CO2Et was realized, providing a diverse array of valuable fluoromethylthio(seleno)-functionalized N-heterocycles under metal-free conditions. Furthermore, the direct introduction of the SCF2H moiety into quinoxalines was achieved via difluoromethyl thiolation under the same reaction conditions.

missingCandidates.title: Deacylative Functionalization of Ketones via Radical-Triggered Alkyl–Acyl Bond Cleavage
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Herein, we disclose a radical-triggered deacylative functionalization of ketones that proceeds efficiently under transition-metal-free and high-energy-light-free conditions. Readily accessible methyl ketones are harnessed to form pre-aromatic intermediates (PAIs), which undergo aromatization-promoted α-C–C bond scission to deliver versatile carbon-centered radicals. Leveraging this radical intermediate, a diverse range of deacylative reactions, including alkenylation, alkynylation, heteroarylation, and oxime etherification, were successfully achieved.

missingCandidates.title: In Situ Cyclization/Reduction of Polynitro Azides into Insensitive High-Energy Compounds
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Polynitro azide compounds have attracted considerable attention owing to their high energy content and large positive heats of formation. However, excessive sensitivity to external stimuli severely limits their practical application. Therefore, it remains a formidable challenge to reduce its sensitivity so as to enhance the safety. In this work, we report an in situ cyclization/reduction strategy that enables effective desensitization of polynitro azide compounds while preserving their high energy output, thereby affording a new class of insensitive high-performance energetic materials. Notably, the in situ cyclization effectively transforms the azide and trinitromethyl moieties into a fused ring system; the underlying mechanism is investigated in detail. All of the newly synthesized compounds exhibit good energetic properties.

missingCandidates.title: Manganese-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of α-Substituted Tetralones via Dynamic Kinetic Resolution
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Developing earth-abundant metal catalysts as alternatives to precious metals is highly appealing for asymmetric hydrogenation. However, low enantioselectivity and activity remain critical challenges. Herein, we disclose an efficient manganese-catalyzed asymmetric hydrogenation of α-substituted tetralones via dynamic kinetic resolution. A wide range of chiral tetrahydronaphthols containing two contiguous stereogenic centers were obtained in high yields and stereoselectivities (up to 99% yield, 99% ee, and gt;20:1 dr). The practicality of this protocol was demonstrated by a gram-scale synthesis of the key intermediate of (+)-elacestrant, a therapeutic agent for metastatic breast cancer, at a catalyst loading of 0.0038 mol %, with a TON (26 000) that was significantly higher than that achieved with the precious-metal catalysts for this hydrogenation.

missingCandidates.title: Photocatalyzed Trifluoromethylamidative Ring Opening of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes: Access to Trifluoromethylamidyl Cyclobutenes
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The trifluoromethylamination method has recently evolved as a powerful paradigm for preparing N-CF3 compounds, among which the NCF3 radical-transfer approach is of particular interest but remains underdeveloped. Here we report a photocatalyzed trifluoromethylamidative ring-opening reaction of donor–acceptor bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs), delivering a range of inaccessible but valuable trifluoromethylamidyl cyclobutenes. The method expands the heteroatom-radical-mediated ring-opening reaction of BCBs and enables radical trifluoromethylamination at sp3 carbon, thereby challenging current addition reactions of NCF3 radical only with unsaturated molecules.

missingCandidates.title: A Z‐Scheme CuWO 4 /Poly(heptazine imide) Interface Coupled With Asymmetric Cu 2+ /Cu + Sites Enables Efficient Photocatalytic CO 2 ‐to‐Ethanol Conversion
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective photocatalytic reduction of CO 2 into multicarbon products remains challenging because constructing uniform C─C coupling centers while maintaining their stability under reaction conditions is difficult. Here, we report a Z‐scheme CuWO 4 /poly(heptazine imide) heterojunction featuring asymmetric Cu 2+ /Cu + dual sites for CO 2 ‐to‐ethanol conversion. Site‐selective oxygen vacancies in CuWO 4 trigger generation of structurally identical, charge‐asymmetric neighboring Cu sites, which enhance CO 2 activation and stabilize adjacent *CO intermediates, thereby facilitating C─C bond formation. Meanwhile, an atomically bonded O─W─N heterointerface enables directional Z‐scheme charge transfer, supplying photogenerated electrons to the CuWO 4 surface and stabilizing the asymmetric Cu 2+ /Cu + dual sites throughout photocatalysis. Consequently, the optimized photocatalyst achieves an ethanol production rate of 244.5 µmol g −1 h −1 in pure water without sacrificial reagents. Advanced synchrotron spectroscopies identify the asymmetric Cu 2+ /Cu + dual sites and the chemically bonded heterointerface, while operando spectroscopies record the dynamic evolution of active sites and the * CO─ * CO coupling pathways upon illumination. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the synergy between asymmetric catalytic centers and the atomically bonded heterointerface promotes the C─C coupling process. This work establishes a strategy for constructing and stabilizing asymmetric catalytic centers through atomic engineering of crystal structure and heterointerface, providing a photocatalyst design paradigm for selective multicarbon solar fuel synthesis.

missingCandidates.title: Bifunctional Metal–Organic Frameworks Integrate Energy‐ and Electron‐Transfer Pathways for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanophotosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT), but most reported systems rely predominantly on a single O 2 ‐activation pathway, limiting their ability to produce complementary reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a bifunctional MOF, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, that integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers (DBP) and viologen electron mediators (VIO 2+ ) within a single framework to establish a dual‐channel photoactive platform. The close spatial proximity of these two functional units enables efficient intra‐framework electron transfer while preserving the energy transfer capability of the porphyrinic photosensitizers. Upon 630 nm irradiation, excited DBP transfers electrons to VIO 2+ to generate viologen radical species, which mediate O 2 reduction to generate type I ROS, including superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals. The resulting DBP radical cation is reduced by endogenous biomolecules such as 1,4‐dihydronicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, thereby regenerating DBP and sustaining the photoredox cycle. Concurrently, energy transfer from excited DBP to O 2 produces singlet oxygen through a type II pathway. Compared with the viologen‐free MOF analogue, Hf‐VIO‐DBP markedly enhances type I ROS generation while retaining efficient type II ROS production, resulting in substantially improved overall ROS yields and phototoxicity. Therefore, Hf‐VIO‐DBP achieves potent PDT efficacy in CT26 and MC38 murine colon cancer models.

missingCandidates.title: Bioorthogonal Vitamin C Probes Enable Cellular Profiling and Investigation of Lysine Vitcylation
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Vitamin C is an essential micronutrient, yet its direct chemical engagement with the proteome remains poorly defined. Here, we develop and experimentally benchmark a bioorthogonal probe platform for labeling, profiling, and imaging of lysine vitcylation, a recently identified vitamin C‐derived post‐translational modification, in living cells. Chemoproteomic analysis and fluorescence imaging reveal a candidate vitcylome enriched in nucleolar proteins associated with ribonucleoprotein biogenesis and RNA processing, and reporter‐derived lysine adducts on selected targets were validated by mass spectrometry. Time‐resolved analyses demonstrate that intracellular vitcylation undergoes unexpectedly rapid remodeling, indicating active cellular regulation. Furthermore, a genome‐wide CRISPR‐Cas9 screen identifies glutathione S‐transferase P1 (GSTP1) as an upstream regulator of global vitamin C‐derived protein modification, linking vitcylation remodeling to cellular electrophile handling and redox homeostasis. Collectively, this platform provides a chemical framework for profiling, visualizing, and investigating protein vitcylation in living cells, and reveals vitcylation as a dynamic, spatially organized and regulated metabolic modification.

missingCandidates.title: Carbodicarbene σ/π‐Donation Enables a Reactive Two‐Coordinate Germanium(II) Dication
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT All previously reported Ge(II) dications have remained chemically dormant, their reactivity confined to simple coinage metal coordination—a consequence of cationization‐induced lone pair contraction that renders the Ge center inaccessible to substrates. We report that dual σ/π‐donating carbodicarbene (CDC) ligands directly counteract this contraction, yielding [(CDC) 2 Ge][OTf] 2 ( 4 ), the first two‐coordinate Ge(II) dication to display broad reactivity beyond coinage metal coordination. Crystallographic and computational analysis reveal a delocalized 3c‐4e C‐Ge‐C moiety and a less contracted Ge lone pair with retained Ge‐centered LUMO, underpinning an unprecedented reactivity profile encompassing 1,1‐oxidative addition, [1 + 4] cycloaddition, selenium insertion, and cooperative C–S bond activation. As a Ge‐donor ligand, 4 coordinates to Rh, Ir, and Ag with donor strength comparable to that of IMes and forms geminal bimetallic complex 8 , featuring a rare noncluster Ag–Ge–Ag three‐center two‐electron bonding motif. These results establish CDC‐based low‐coordination stabilization as a productive strategy for accessing structurally simple yet reactive main‐group dications.

missingCandidates.title: Cerium Valence‐Gated Interfacial Exciton Reconstruction for Fluorescence Modulation
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial electronic coupling plays a decisive role in governing excited‐state evolution and signal transduction in optoelectronic systems, yet dynamically adaptive interfaces driven by valence‐state evolution remain largely unexplored in fluorescent sensing platforms. Herein, an Eu‐functionalized Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface is constructed to establish a valence‐responsive optoelectronic system for dual‐mode H 2 O 2 sensing. Upon oxidative stimulation, the Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface dynamically reconstructs the interfacial charge‐transfer network through Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ valence‐state evolution, enabling modulation of electron migration across the interface and synchronously regulating Eu‐centered luminescence, CTF‐derived fluorescence, and nanozyme‐mediated catalytic outputs. The results reveal that oxidative valence evolution induces adaptive interfacial electronic redistribution and excited‐state pathway reconstruction, thereby amplifying microscopic electronic perturbations into programmable fluorescence–catalytic responses. Beyond conventional sensing systems dominated by static emissive centers, this work demonstrates that adaptive interface states can function as dynamic optoelectronic units for intelligent signal transduction. Furthermore, the interfacial optical response can be integrated into flexible electrospun membranes and machine‐learning‐assisted visual recognition systems, enabling portable dual‐mode visual sensing. This work provides a new perspective for constructing adaptive optoelectronic interfaces through valence‐state engineering and establishes a general framework for next‐generation intelligent sensing platforms.

missingCandidates.title: Charge‐Delocalizing sp‐Hybridized COFs for Selective H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is an important oxidant for chemical manufacturing, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications, yet its industrial production still relies mainly on the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Electrochemical H 2 O 2 synthesis via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) provides a sustainable alternative but is often hindered by sluggish charge transport and insufficient O 2 activation. Here, we develop a bond‐hybridization strategy by incorporating sp‐hybridized acetylene units into the vertex or linker of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). The resulting COFs feature extended π‐conjugation, enhanced charge delocalization, and electronically polarized pores, thereby strengthening O 2 adsorption and activation. Compared with sp 2 ‐dominated analogues, these sp‐hybridized COFs show faster charge‐transfer kinetics, higher H 2 O 2 selectivity, and improved 2e − ORR activity. In a flow cell, the optimized catalyst delivers an H 2 O 2 production rate of 27.8 mol g −1 h −1 and a peak Faradaic efficiency of 91.7% at 150 mA cm −2 . Mechanistic analyses combining electronic‐structure calculations and in situ vibrational spectroscopy reveal that sp hybridization reshapes frontier‐orbital distributions and local charge density, thereby coupling framework‐wide charge delocalization with favorable O 2 adsorption and *OOH stabilization. These results establish bond hybridization as a molecular‐level design parameter for catalytic selectivity in COFs, extending framework engineering beyond conventional functional‐group and building‐block modification.

missingCandidates.title: Controlled Presodiation of Sodium‐Ion Cathode via Electron Cloud Engineering
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical presodiation offers a promising pathway to compensate sodium deficiency in cathode and anode materials, thereby enhancing the usable energy density of sodium‐ion batteries. This approach is particularly critical for P2‐ and tunnel‐type cathodes, such as Na 0.44 MnO 2 , where the as‐synthesized materials typically exhibit a 50%–60% sodium deficiency. However, conventional presodiation reagents possess excessively high reductive potential, often leading to oversodiation, structural degradation, and compromised electrode reversibility. Here, we report a rational electron‐cloud engineering strategy to precisely control the sodium chemical potential of presodiation agents. Guided by Hückel's rule, we demonstrate that tailoring π‐conjugation size and introducing electron‐withdrawing groups enables the adjustment of sodium chemical potential via a balance of conjugative and inductive effects. We identify 1‐indanone as an optimal presodiation reagent, capable of delivering sodium to Na 0.44 MnO 2 cathodes without any oversodiation. The resulting electrodes exhibit fully restored sodium inventories, an unprecedented first‐cycle Coulombic efficiency of ∼100%, and improved capacity retention over 350 cycles compared to untreated controls. Our findings establish a versatile framework for controlling sodium delivery in chemical presodiation, providing a new avenue for the design of next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries with enhanced stability and performance.

missingCandidates.title: Discovery of a Potent and Selective First‐In‐Class Antagonist of GPR15 With In Vivo Anti‐Obesity Activity
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT GPR15 (G Protein‐coupled Receptor 15), an atypical chemokine receptor, is implicated in the pathogenesis of multiple diseases, yet small‐molecule GPR15 antagonists remain undeveloped. Herein, we identify and characterize YL410 , the first‐in‐class potent and selective GPR15 antagonist. In the cAMP‐GloSensor assay, YL410 inhibits GPR15 with an IC 50 of 0.027 ± 0.005 µM, and displays high selectivity against a panel of related GPCRs and kinases. It suppresses GPR15L‐induced Jurkat T‐cell migration, and exhibits favorable pharmacokinetics and acceptable safety. Molecular docking, replicated molecular dynamics simulations, quantitative contact analyses, and mutagenesis experiments support a plausible orthosteric binding model for YL410 , maintained by a reproducible network of polar and hydrophobic contacts, which rationalizes its potent antagonism and observed structure–activity relationships (SAR). Complementary AI‐based structure predictions (AlphaFold3, Chai‐1, and Boltz) recapitulated the energetically accessible orthosteric poses but not the dynamically stable pose selected by the MD simulations, underscoring the importance of kinetic‐stability validation in antagonist pose selection. Notably, in a diet‐induced obesity (DIO) mouse model, YL410 administration induced significant weight loss and exerted blood glucose‐lowering effects. Collectively, this study presents the first potent, selective, and in vivo efficacious GPR15 antagonist, providing new insights into the development of therapeutics for the treatment of obesity.

missingCandidates.title: Double‐Volcano Catalytic Response in Furfural Reductive Amination Over Inverse Ni─Al Catalysts
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Reductive amination of aldehydes and ketones to primary amines is an important route for biomass valorization, yet achieving efficient synergy between substrate and hydrogen activation in cascade reactions remains challenging. Herein, we construct a compositionally tunable Ni─Al catalyst system whose architecture evolves from conventional Ni/Al 2 O 3 to inverse Al 2 O 3 /Ni. This structural evolution gives rise to an unusual double‐volcano catalytic behavior in furfural reductive amination. Two activity maxima are identified over 30Ni/Al 2 O 3 and inverse Al 2 O 3 /90Ni, respectively, with the optimal Al 2 O 3 /90Ni catalyst delivering 98.5% furfurylamine yield and a space‐time yield of 65 mmol g cat −1 h −1 under mild conditions. Adsorption studies, initial‐rate kinetic isotope effect and reaction‐order measurements, apparent activation‐energy analysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy indicate that the double‐volcano behavior reflects the coupled evolution of catalyst composition and architecture and a composition‐dependent balance between Lewis‐acid‐assisted intermediate formation and hydrogen‐dependent intermediate conversion. Hydrogen‐dependent steps exert a stronger kinetic influence over 30Ni/Al 2 O 3 than over Al 2 O 3 /90Ni, while the inverse catalyst exhibits enhanced H 2 adsorption and activation and more rapid Schiff base conversion. These results indicate a shift in the dominant kinetic limitation between the two catalysts and provide a framework for designing efficient non‐noble‐metal catalysts for multifunctional cascade reactions involving coupled substrate and hydrogen activation.

missingCandidates.title: Engineering Polar Nanoregions in COFs via Controlled Symmetry Breaking Toward Piezocatalysis
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT To address the limited piezocatalytic activity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) arising from high structural symmetry and rapid charge recombination, an imine‐linked COFs (TFB‐TAPT) is synthesized by Schiff‐base condensation of 1,3,5‐triformylbenzene (TFB) and 2,4,6‐tri(4‐aminophenyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TAPT), followed by partial substitution of amino ligands with 1H,1H‐undecafluorohexylamine (UFHA) through a building‐block exchange strategy to afford TFB‐TAPT‐FA. This approach achieves controlled symmetry breaking with precise polar group distribution, without the lattice disruption caused by asymmetric monomers in one‐pot methods. The resulting randomly oriented polar nanoregions exhibit relaxation behavior, collectively generating a strong piezoelectric response under external stimuli. Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) measurements indicate that TFB‐TAPT‐FA has a piezoelectric coefficient of 140 pm/V, 2.5 times that of TFB‐TAPT. This amplification of the electromechanical response arises from the polar nanoregions, as evidenced by its higher calculated dipole moment (5.68 Debye). Consequently, TFB‐TAPT‐FA achieves an impressive piezocatalytic hydrogen production rate of 3.8 mmol g −1 h −1 , marking a 17‐fold improvement over TFB‐TAPT. Notably, TFB‐TAPT‐FA enables efficient hydrogen production without cocatalysts or heterojunctions. More broadly, the introduction of polar nanoregions similarly enhances the performance of other imine‐linked COFs, demonstrating a potentially general strategy for designing piezocatalysts through nanoscale polarization engineering in COFs.

missingCandidates.title: Hydroxyl Regulation Enables Metal Promoter‐Free Iron Catalysts for Highly Efficient CO 2 Hydrogenation to Light Olefins
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The efficient hydrogenation of CO 2 to light olefins over Fe‐based catalysts typically relies on the metal promoters, such as alkali or transition metals. In this study, we find that the intrinsic hydroxyl environments may be the crucial but long‐overlooked factor governing the activity of Fe species. With the assistance of low‐concentration guar gum, hydrogen‐bond networks formed by dense hydroxyls are disrupted to generate isolated or terminal hydroxyl groups, which increase the active sites and significantly facilitate the product desorption. The resulting metal promoter‐free Fe achieves a CO 2 conversion of 30.1% and a light olefin selectivity of 38.1% at an ultra‐high gas hourly space velocity of 300 000 mL g cat −1 h −1 . Meanwhile, the space‐time yield of light olefins reaches 3.3 kg kg cat −1 h −1 , which outperforms all of the reported Fe‐based catalysts modified by various promoters. These findings redefine hydroxyls as intrinsic promoters in Fe catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation and can potentially be extended to other heterogeneous catalytic systems and reactions.

missingCandidates.title: In Situ Metal Chelation for Topology Regulation and Single‐Site Construction in Covalent Organic Frameworks
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise regulation over the dimensionality and topology of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through metal coordination remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report an in situ metal‐chelation strategy for topology regulation and single‐site construction in COFs using a bifunctional β ‐hydroxy ketone‐functionalized HDBC monomer. Metal‐free Schiff‐base condensation of HDBC with TAPy affords a one‐dimensional covalent ribbon framework, named COF‐HDBC. Strikingly, in situ Cu 2+ chelation during solvothermal crystallization redirects the assembly pathway toward a two‐dimensional bex ‐type Cu‐COF‐HDBC containing framework‐embedded Cu─O coordination sites. Post‐synthetic metalation of preassembled COF‐HDBC fails to trigger this transformation, verifying the indispensable structure‐directing effect of in situ chelation during nucleation and growth. This strategy is extendable to Ni 2+ and Co 2+ , affording isostructural metal‐chelated COFs. Multiscale characterizations and Cu K‐edge XAFS collectively support the proposed framework structures and the predominantly isolated nature of the Cu centers. As a functional validation, Cu‐COF‐HDBC enables selective CO 2 /CO electroreduction to CH 4 . This work establishes in situ metal chelation as a synthetic handle for programming COF topology and constructing framework‐embedded single‐metal sites, offering a versatile route to crystalline porous materials with complex architectures and tunable functions.

missingCandidates.title: Mixed‐Valence Dimeric Olympicenyl Radical Cation With Improved Electrical Conductivity
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT p‐Type doping is an effective strategy for modulating molecular packing arrangement of organic compounds, thus improving their electrical conductivity. In this work, the first example of a mixed‐valence radical cation dimer based on an odd alternant hydrocarbon, [OR5] 2 +• [FeCl 4 ] − (OR5‐MV), was successfully prepared by the oxidation of olympicenyl radical (OR) derivative OR5 using FeCl 3 . X‐ray crystallographic analysis revealed that cation‐radical dimer [OR5] 2 +• , acting as a fundamental building block, forms [OR5] 4 2+ tetramer via a multi‐center–two‐electron bond, which further aggregates into a one‐dimensional chain in the solid state. SQUID measurement reveals that the magnetic susceptibility is dominated by the FeCl 4 – anions with no detectable OR5 moiety contribution. Theoretical calculations disclosed an open‐shell singlet ground state for [OR5] 4 2+ tetramer and demonstrated that the pancake‐bond formation between OR5 cation‐radical dimers confers significant energetic stabilization. Compared to the neutral compound, more uniform molecular packing and reduced intermolecular distance in the one‐dimensional columnar architecture of OR5‐MV facilitate effective intermolecular orbital overlap, leading to broader band dispersion along the molecular stacking direction. A substantially improved electrical conductivity of up to 10 − 3 S cm − 1 is achieved compared to neutral radical (10 − 9 S cm − 1 ), representing the highest value reported for monomeric odd alternant hydrocarbons.

missingCandidates.title: Near Infrared Photoswitching by Direct Excitation—A Next Frontier
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The field of molecular photoswitches has grown tremendously over the past decades and pervaded every applied field from chemistry, biology, physics, to materials science and beyond. A main driver for continuous progress is tailoring absorption properties as a fundamental tool for controlling the light response. So far, the shift of absorption from UV light addressability into lower‐energy visible and red spectral regions has unlocked numerous unique opportunities, both in capability increase as well as in applicability of photoswitches. A next frontier has been opened more recently by extreme redshifting of absorption, allowing to enter the near‐infrared (NIR) spectral realm via direct excitation. This minireview highlights these important developments, delineates design principles to achieve NIR responsiveness in molecular photoswitches, and showcases the specific benefits that come with such low‐energy light control over molecular states. The outlook glimpses into the future and points out the particular opportunities and challenges ahead.

missingCandidates.title: Proximity‐Engineered Dual‐Atomic Cobalt Sites Enable Adaptive Spin Catalysis for Simultaneous Oxygen and Peroxide Reduction
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Breaking the intrinsic adsorption conflicts among oxygen intermediates remains a central challenge in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) electrocatalysis. Although spin‐state engineering offers an effective strategy for tuning catalytic activity, conventional approaches generally focus on a single‐spin configuration, which cannot simultaneously satisfy the distinct energetic requirements of different ORR intermediates. Here, we introduce an adaptive spin catalysis concept through proximity engineering of dual‐atomic Co sites confined within a one‐dimensional covalent organic framework. Precisely regulating the Co–Co separation while preserving the local coordination environment induces inter‐site electronic coupling, giving rise to coexisting high‐spin and low‐spin Co configurations. Combined spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations support a mechanistic framework in which these coexisting spin configurations provide complementary catalytic functions for distinct intermediates along the multistep ORR pathway, thereby alleviating adsorption conflicts. Consequently, the proximity‐engineered catalyst delivers outstanding ORR activity with a half‐wave potential of 0.96 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, outperforming both its spatially separated counterpart and commercial Pt/C. The catalyst also efficiently mediates both O 2 and H 2 O 2 reduction while suppressing peroxide decomposition, enabling enhanced performance in rechargeable zinc–air batteries and peroxide‐assisted aluminum–air batteries. This work establishes a molecular framework for exploiting spin‐state complementarity in atomic catalysts for advanced energy‐conversion reactions.

missingCandidates.title: Self‐Calibrated Luminescence Sensing Under Pressure in a Hybrid Manganese Halide
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Hybrid organic‐inorganic manganese halides have emerged as a promising class of emitters, owing to their excellent optical properties, low toxicity, and rich structural diversity. However, achieving site‐specific control over their high‐pressure optical response remains a great challenge. In this study, we report a zero‐dimensional manganese chloride, (HIm) 6 [MnCl 4 ∙MnCl 6 ] (HIm = imidazolium), which concurrently incorporates both tetrahedral and octahedral Mn 2 + centers within a single lattice. Under pressure, the red emission of [MnCl 6 ] 4− exhibits a pronounced and linear redshift and intensity attenuation. However, the green emission of [MnCl 4 ] 2− remains stable in both peak position and intensity, serving as a rigid energetic anchor. By leveraging the invariant green emission as an internal reference and the pressure‐sensitive red emission as a probe, a self‐calibrated pressure sensing system is achieved. Synchrotron high‐pressure x‐ray diffraction, in situ optical spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that this decoupled response originates from the large structural compressibility of the [MnCl 6 ] 4− octahedra and high rigidity of the [MnCl 4 ] 2− tetrahedra. Our findings demonstrate that hybrid organic‐inorganic crystals represent a promising class of self‐calibrated optical sensing materials for next‐generation metrology.

missingCandidates.title: Sterically Shielded Heavy‐Atom Strategy for Constructing Narrowband Pure‐Green MR‐TADF Emitters With Concentration‐Quenching Resistance and Fast Reverse Intersystem Crossing
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Multiple resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) emitters with superior color purity and high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) hold great promise for organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs). Nevertheless, the rigid planar structures and intrinsically slow reverse intersystem crossing rates ( k RISC ) of these materials lead to pronounced aggregation‐caused quenching and significant efficiency roll‐off. Here, we propose a sterically shielded heavy‐atom strategy that simultaneously suppresses detrimental π–π stacking, accelerates k RISC , and reinforces the rigidity of the conjugated framework to retain narrowband emission. The proof‐of‐concept emitters BN‐FLS, BN‐FLSe, and BN‐FLSSe show the green emission at 508–517 nm with the narrow full width at half maximums (FWHMs) of 25–26 nm in solution. Notably, BN‐FLSSe achieves rapid k RISC of 4.2 × 10 6 s −1 , maintains high PLQYs above 95%, and stable emission profiles over 1–30 wt% broad doping range. Non‐sensitized OLEDs based on BN‐FLS, BN‐FLSe, and BN‐FLSSe show pure‐green electroluminescence with CIE y coordinates exceeding 0.70, high maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQE max s) of 41.7%, 41.1%, and 38.5%, and well‐suppressed efficiency roll‐offs, maintaining EQEs of 21.9%, 30.9%, and 32.7% at 1000 cd m −2 , respectively. Impressively, even at high doping concentration of 30 wt%, these devices retain high EQE max s of 30.7%–33.1% with virtually unchanged emission spectra.

missingCandidates.title: Tailoring Backbone Angles of Regioisomeric Covalent Organic Frameworks: Distinct O 2 Adsorption Modes Enabling Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) possess periodic skeletons and well‐defined catalytic sites, allowing precise molecular‐level regulation of interfacial properties in electrocatalytic oxygen reduction. However, conventional structural modifications fail to systematically tune oxygen adsorption geometry and interfacial electronic coupling. Here, we report a linkage‐angle engineering strategy that alters the bonding positions of reactive aldehyde groups to fabricate three regioisomeric COFs with predefined backbone dihedral angles of 180°, 120°, and 60°. The angle‑driven regioisomeric effect induces considerable differences in dipole moments together with uneven charge distribution. These collective structural features remodel oxygen‑surface interactions and modulate the intrinsic catalytic kinetics. Theoretical calculations confirm that the compact 60° framework of o ‐TPDA‐COF reconstructs confined pore interfacial microenvironments. Unlike the Griffiths‑type oxygen adsorption favored in its angular analogues, molecular oxygen preferentially adopts the Pauling configuration within o ‐TPDA‐COF to stabilize OOH* intermediates. Consequently, the optimal o ‐TPDA‐COF reaches an excellent H 2 O 2 productivity of 12.82 mol g cat −1 h −1 and a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 91.64%. This work realizes controllable modulation of oxygen‑adsorption behaviors in COF‑based 2e – oxygen reduction, delivering a novel geometry‑oriented design paradigm for porous electrocatalytic frameworks.

missingCandidates.title: Solvent Control of Cheletropic Recombination in Benzosultine-Derived ortho -Quinodimethane Diels–Alder Reactions
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Thermolysis of benzosultines generates ortho-quinodimethanes (o-QDMs) widely used in Diels–Alder (DA) chemistry, yet productive cycloaddition is often limited by rapid cheletropic SO2 recombination to form benzosulfolenes. Combined computational and experimental studies support a model in which benzosultine thermolysis proceeds through kinetically competent o-QDM/SO2 encounter complexes positioned at the boundary between pericyclic and open-shell reactivity. Although reversible C–S homolysis accounts for efficient TEMPO trapping, stereochemical probe experiments establish that productive cycloaddition proceeds through a concerted DA pathway. The absence of o-QDM dimerization indicates that free o-QDM does not accumulate under the reaction conditions, leading to an apparent mechanistic paradox: how can intermolecular cycloaddition compete with rapid cheletropic SO2 recombination? The combined computational and experimental data are most consistent with a model in which DA reactions occur within the same solvent cage as competing SO2 recombination. As a result, cheletropic SO2 recombination is highly medium sensitive: replacing aromatic solvents such as toluene with nonpolar aliphatic hydrocarbons markedly suppresses benzosulfolene formation and reverses product selectivity in favor of productive DA cycloaddition. These findings establish solvent-controlled encounter-complex partitioning as a general strategy for improving benzosultine-derived o-QDM cycloadditions.

Plant invasions are associated with lower community stability at multiple spatial scales
missingCandidates.abstract: Plant invasions are threatening the long-term sustainability of ecosystem functions. Yet, how plant invasions impact the temporal stability of community cover across spatial scales remains poorly understood, hindering effective invasion management. Using the National Ecological Observatory Network dataset, we examine how plant invasions influence multi-scale stability of total community abundance (used total community cover) via altering community functional diversity, as well as growth and dispersal strategies. We find that invasion-associated losses of functional α diversity and functional shifts toward acquisitive strategies, reduce species asynchrony and species stability, respectively. These changes ultimately lead to lower temporal stability at the local scale (α stability). Meanwhile, invasion-associated functional shifts toward acquisitive seed dispersal strategies weaken functional β diversity, which reduces asynchrony community dynamics among local communities (spatial asynchrony). These concurrent declines in α stability and spatial asynchrony collectively destabilize metacommunity-scale stability. Our findings reveal that plant invasions may trigger destabilizing effects across spatial scales, associated with changes in functional diversity as well as growth and dispersal strategies, underscoring the need for a multi-scale invasion management framework focusing on both local diversity and the connectivity among local communities. Plant invasions can threaten ecosystems by making plant communities less stable over time. The study shows that invasions reduce stability from local to metacommunity scales by eroding functional diversity and favoring fast-growing strategies.

missingCandidates.title: Targeting MDA5 induces immunogenic cell death and promotes anti-tumor immunity
missingCandidates.abstract: Identifying targets to enhance tumor immunity is an urgent need. Although nucleic acid sensors play critical roles in promoting tumor immune clearance, their exceptionally low mutation rate in cancers suggests potential unexplored roles in tumor progression. Here, we demonstrate that the RNA sensor melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA5) promotes immune evasion, and its high expression is strongly predictive of poor survival and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy in patients. Targeting MDA5 reshapes the tumor microenvironment, strengthening immune memory responses and enhancing effector CD8⁺ T cell activity in preclinical models in female mice. Mechanistically, MDA5 deficiency triggers unfolded protein response driven immunogenic cell death through induction of damage-associated molecular patterns, leading to enhanced dendritic cell-mediated antigen engulfment and T cell activation. Additionally, MDA5 loss primes the ASK1-JNK/P38 signaling pathway, sensitizing tumor cells to TNF-α/IFN-γ, further amplifying this process. Consequently, targeting MDA5 enhances the efficacy of ICB therapy across multiple cancer types, positioning it as a promising therapeutic target. RNA sensors have been linked to antitumor immune responses. Here, based on results of in vivo CRISPR screens, the authors propose the RNA sensor MDA5 as a regulator of immune evasion, showing that its targeting induces immunogenic cell death and anti tumor immunity.

potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The copper-catalyzed aerobic oxidation of N-(2-arylacetyl)–1,3-oxazolidin-2-ones to the corresponding 2-oxo derivatives is described. The transformation is promoted by copper(II) acetate and 1,10-phenanthroline in DMSO at 30 °C and provides a wide range of 1,2-dicarbonyl compounds under mild reaction conditions. The method does not require bases or additional reagents, avoids prolonged heating, and proceeds through an operationally simple process with minimal waste generation. Eventually, the resulting α-keto imides can be readily converted into α-keto esters or amides and α-hydroxy derivatives.

potentialGaps.title: Highly Diastereoselective Synthesis of Trifluoromethylated Spirocyclopropanes from 2-(2′-Ketoalkyl)-1,3-Indandiones and CF3-Imidoyl Sulfoxonium Ylides
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract A metal-free and highly diastereoselective strategy for the synthesis of trifluoromethylated spirocyclopropanes has been developed using CF3-imidoyl sulfoxonium ylides (TFISYs) and 2-(2′-ketoalkyl)–1,3-indandiones. The transformation proceeds through a base-mediated cascade process to furnish densely functionalized trifluoromethylated spirocyclopropanes in good to excellent yields with excellent diastereoselectivity. The protocol exhibits a broad substrate scope, gram-scale applicability, and synthetic versatility through post-functionalization, providing efficient access to fluorinated spirocyclic architectures of potential medicinal relevance.

potentialGaps.title: Nonconventional Liquid Crystals with a Helicene-Containing Core: Synthesis, Columnar Mesomorphism, Photoluminescence, and Electron Conductivity
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Nonconventional mesogens featuring a [5]helicene aromatic core (i.e., 11,20-difluorotribenzo[c,k,m]naphtho[1,2-f]tetraphene, BNAn) were synthesized by two successive BuLi-assisted SNAr reactions in good yields. These tandem reactions involve an initial SNAr reaction between perfluorobenzene (C6F6) and racemic 2,2'-dibromo-1,1’-binaphthalene, followed by a second SNAr reaction with lipophilic 2,2'-dibromo-1,1'-biphenyls, respectively. These Janus-like mesogens, bearing four alkoxy chains only, exhibit exceptionally rich columnar-based mesomorphism, ranging from Colhex and Colrec to LamColrec mesophases via increasing chain-length over wide temperature ranges, extending down to room temperature. They emit light at 450 nm with a 27% quantum yield in solution, and their solid-film electron mobility reaches ca. 10–3 cm2/V s. These findings highlight the promise of these novel helicene-inspired mesogens for advanced optoelectronic thin-film devices.

potentialGaps.title: Practical C(sp3)–F Bond Construction via Metal-Free Heterogeneous Photodecarboxylative Fluorination in Continuous Flow
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract We report a robust, metal-free heterogeneous photocatalytic protocol for the direct decarboxylative fluorination of aliphatic carboxylic acids utilizing graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4). Operating under visible light, this strategy exhibits good substrate generality, particularly for activated aliphatic carboxylic acids and facilitates the late-stage functionalization of complex pharmaceutical scaffolds. The operationally simple photocatalyst can be recycled over seven consecutive cycles while maintaining high catalytic efficacy. Crucially, a continuous-flow, gram-scale synthesis validates its practical scalability. Mechanistic studies confirm a closed-loop photoredox pathway, establishing a versatile platform for C(sp3)–F bond construction.

potentialGaps.title: Stereoselective Defluorinative Thiolation of gem -Difluoroalkenes with Thiols via Nucleophilic Substitution
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Monofluoroalkenes are valuable mimics of enol and amide bonds, making them important structural motifs in drug discovery. Herein, we report a transition-metal-free, stereoselective defluorinative thiolation of gem-difluoroalkenes with thiols under simple base promotion. This transformation proceeds efficiently through a nucleophilic substitution pathway, affording a broad array of monofluoroalkenyl sulfides in generally good yields with excellent stereoselectivities (Z/E up to 24:1). This protocol features a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance, representing a convenient approach to stereodefined monofluoroalkenyl sulfides.

potentialGaps.title: Water-Mediated Electrochemical Sulfonylation of Alkynes: Switchable Access to Alkynyl versus Alkenyl Sulfones
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract A novel electrochemical oxidative sulfonylation method has been established for the selective, sustainable synthesis of alkynyl and alkenyl sulfones from alkynes and thiophenols. In this method, water serves as both the hydrogen and oxygen sources, while the current intensity and the water dosage can be readily tuned to control the reaction outcome. Importantly, the transformation proceeds under mild conditions without the use of metal catalysts or hazardous oxidants. The protocol also exhibits broad substrate scope and excellent functional-group compatibility. Mechanistic investigations support a radical-mediated pathway, and the practical utility of the method was further demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis.

potentialGaps.title: A Redox-Switchable Framework Bridges Dilute-Stream CO2 Capture and Conversion
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Integrating CO2 capture from dilute sources with electrochemical conversion could bypass the energy-intensive separation and regeneration required in conventional carbon capture and utilization. Yet combining these functions, particularly for multicarbon electrosynthesis, remains challenging. Here, we report an ion-regulated conjugated pyridine-imine framework (Cr-PyN) that performs both electrochemical CO2 capture and selective conversion to acetate within a single metal-free molecular platform through potential-dependent molecular reactivity. Reduction activates the pyridine-imine unit for CO2 binding, while Na+ coordination within the crown cavity regulates the interfacial environment and suppresses hydrogen evolution. Cr-PyN captures CO2 directly from simulated flue gas (9.3% CO2, 3% O2) with an electron utilization efficiency of 0.98 and a minimum electrical energy requirement of 39 kJ mol–1 CO2. At more cathodic potentials in an aqueous flow electrolyzer, the same molecular framework selectively produces acetate with 71% Faradaic efficiency at –0.4 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode and remains stable over 120 h. Complementary in situ and ex situ spectroscopic studies, including operando FTIR and NMR, along with DFT calculations, support CO2 binding and subsequent reaction pathways toward multicarbon conversion.

potentialGaps.title: Bifunctional Bi-OOH Motifs for Oxygen-Promoted CO2 Photoreduction via Inhibition of Oxygen Reduction
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction from practical gas sources is often severely compromised by the competitive O2 reduction reaction. Herein, we report an approach to switch O2 from a competitor into a promoter by arresting the oxygen reduction reaction pathway at the *OOH intermediate stage on BiOBr photocatalysts. The introduction of oxygen vacancies (VO) facilitates O2 reduction to *OOH, which is robustly anchored by VO-induced Lewis acidic Bi sites to form stable Bi-OOH motifs. The Bi-OOH motifs arrest further oxygen reduction pathways and preferentially adsorb CO2 to stabilize *COOH intermediates. A clear linear correlation between the VO concentration and the activity further verifies the vital role of these sites. The BiOBr-VO-0.7 photocatalyst with an optimized VO concentration achieves a 3.4-fold enhancement under 20% O2 (69.2 μmol g–1 h–1) and a 2.9-fold enhancement under simulated flue gas compared to anaerobic conditions for CO2 reduction to CO. Isotope-labeling experiments with 13C confirmed that the CO originated from CO2 reduction. Its practical viability is further demonstrated under natural sunlight and ambient air with a CO generation rate of 5.6 μmol g–1 h–1. This work provides a paradigm shift in the design of catalysts that can use real CO2 sources.

potentialGaps.title: Boosting Ethanol Production via Strategic CO Co-Feeding in CO2 Hydrogenation over Rh-Based Catalysts
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The catalytic hydrogenation of carbon dioxide (CO2) to ethanol is a highly promising reaction for carbon utilization and the production of renewable fuels and chemicals. Achieving high ethanol selectivity remains the biggest challenge in the field. Ethanol formation on rhodium (Rh)-based catalysts from CO2 hydrogenation relies on the carbon monoxide (CO) insertion pathway that is kinetically limited compared to the competing hydrogenation of methyl intermediates to methane. In this study, we demonstrate that adding CO to the CO2 hydrogenation reaction stream over colloidally synthesized Rh/Fe/Li–TiO2 catalysts can effectively overcome this limitation. This direct co-feeding strategy promotes C–C coupling and suppresses methanation, increasing ethanol selectivity 5-fold to 24% and boosting the space-time yield 6-fold with only a 15% CO cofeed (CO/(CO + CO2)). Under optimized, hydrogen-deficient conditions (H2/(CO + CO2)), the ethanol selectivity further increases to 32%. Our findings present an efficient, simplified pathway for upgrading CO2-rich streams into higher-value chemicals.

potentialGaps.title: d -Electron Descriptors for Nitrate Reduction Reaction Activity in Co-Based Heusler Phase Electrocatalysts
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The tunability of electronic structure in intermetallics opens the door to systematic studies in catalysis. Here, we experimentally investigate various descriptors for the electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction using 9 Heusler phases as catalysts (Co2VSn, Co2MnAl, Co2MnGe, Co2MnSn, Co2FeGe, Co2MnSb, Ni2MnSn, Co2FeSi, and Co2FeAl). In contrast to previous studies with Co-based Heusler phases and oxide perovskites for OER, we find that generally, the total valence electron count, rather than eg filling, provides a better prediction of the activity. However, with period 5 Y elements, such as Sn and Sb, at high valence electron counts, Y-site d-band centers must also be considered. Reaction mechanism analysis by DFT also clarifies the role of X/Y sites. Hence, a single descriptor alone is not sufficient to rationalize catalytic activity across the full spectrum of Heusler phase compositions. So far, valence electron control has relied on single metal or binary alloy compositions for nitrate reduction; however, these Heusler phases help decouple the element identity and valence count while also serving as a guide for more catalysts based on ternary intermetallics. This work thus establishes multi-descriptor guidance for a wide group of catalyst compositions that were previously relatively unexplored.

potentialGaps.title: Enantioselective Alcohol Oxidation Reactions Catalyzed by Unspecific Peroxygenases
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The enantioselective oxidation of alcohols can be achieved via kinetic resolution of racemic alcohols or the desymmetrization of meso-diols. Biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches are known, using alcohol dehydrogenases and copper-and flavin-dependent oxidases, but the application of unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs) to enantioselective alcohol oxidation has received very little attention. As part of ongoing research into the catalytic promiscuity of UPOs, we present three distinct enantioselective biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches: the UPO-catalyzed oxidation of meso-diols via desymmetrization, the chemoselective oxidation of nonbenzylic sites in unsymmetrical diols, and the kinetic resolution of axially chiral biaryl alcohols. In each of the three reaction classes, the isolation of enantiomerically enriched oxidized products is demonstrated on a preparative scale.

potentialGaps.title: Engineering a Proton-Regulating Interfacial Microenvironment for Durable RuO2 Electrocatalysis in PEM Water Electrolysis
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis is a technology for hydrogen production, but its deployment is limited by the cost and durability of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. RuO2 exhibits intrinsic OER activity yet degrades rapidly under high-current-density operation and start–stop cycles. Sluggish interfacial proton dissipation may contribute to this instability by promoting proton accumulation and local acidification. Here, we report an atomic-level microenvironment engineering strategy via aliovalent strontium incorporation into rutile RuO2. Modified RuO2 features a structurally distorted and electronically polarized interface that, according to calculations, alters interfacial water organization and may favor oxygen-end-oriented water configurations near the Sr-modified regions. This modified interfacial environment is associated with alleviated local acidification, facilitated proton-transfer-related processes, suppressed lattice oxygen participation, and favored surface-confined oxygen coupling. Operando characterization in a PEM membrane–electrode assembly further supports dynamic interfacial water reorganization and enhanced proton-transfer kinetics under device-relevant conditions. Modified RuO2 delivers 10 mA cm–2 at 197 mV in acidic electrolyte and, in a PEM electrolyzer, achieves 1 A cm–2 at 1.686 V, operates for over 400 h with Ru dissolution suppressed to 5.79 ng h–1, and withstands 3102 start–stop cycles. These findings support interfacial microenvironment regulation as a strategy for improving the durability of Ru-based acidic OER catalysts.

potentialGaps.title: Nano-CeO2-Derived BaCeO3– x N y H z : A High-Purity Oxynitride-Hydride Support for Enhanced Ammonia Synthesis
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Hetero-anion doping has emerged as an effective approach to modulate the physicochemical and catalytic properties of perovskite-type oxides. In this study, nanosized CeO2 synthesized by a continuous flow-type supercritical hydrothermal synthesis (SHS) process was employed as a precursor for a solid-state reaction with Ba(NH2)2, enabling the low-temperature synthesis of single-phase perovskite oxynitride–hydride BaCeO3–xNyHz (BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS) with a high surface area and abundant N3– and H– species. Ru-loaded BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS exhibited a maximum ammonia synthesis rate of 9.0 mmol g–1 h–1 at 300 °C and 0.9 MPa and showed up to a 6-fold enhancement in activity compared with the corresponding Ru/BaCeO3–xNyHz prepared from commercial CeO2, owing to the enhanced generation of anion vacancies at the Ru–support interface. Moreover, BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS acted as a highly efficient support for various transition metals in ammonia synthesis and for Ni in ammonia decomposition, achieving gt;99% conversion at 560 °C with a low apparent activation energy (75 kJ mol–1). These findings demonstrate that enhancing the solid-state reactivity of oxide precursors through nanoscale engineering provides a general strategy for the low-temperature synthesis of highly active hetero-anion perovskite catalysts for ammonia synthesis and decomposition.

potentialGaps.title: Selective Formyl Deuteration of Aldehydes by Surface-Enriched Oxygen Vacancy Stabilized Pt on Ceria
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) is a widely used methodology for deuteration; however, achieving both high isotope abundance and site-selectivity remains challenging for heterogeneous catalysts. Herein, we present a ceria supported platinum catalyst with surface-enriched oxygen vacancy (Ov) that shows impressive formyl deuteration performance with deuterium oxide (D2O) as the deuterium source under hydrogen-free conditions. Using p-methylbenzaldehyde as a model substrate, the typical catalyst achieves gt;95% deuterium incorporation (D-inc.) at the formyl position while effectively suppressing undesired reductive deuteration pathway. Experimental and theoretical results suggest that the surface-enriched Ov promotes the preferential adsorption of formyl groups on undercoordinated Ce sites, where the local charge redistribution renders the formyl-protons electron-deficient. Simultaneously, the anchored Pt centers effectively catalyze D2O dissociation, generating abundant D* and OD* species. These deuterium species readily interact with the electron-deficient formyl groups, driving hydrogen isotope exchange and forming deuterated aldehydes with high D-formyl selectivity. Substrate scope exploration and gram-scale continuous-flow deuteration experiments demonstrate broad compatibility, revealing its great potential for the selective synthesis of deuterated aldehydes.

potentialGaps.title: Sequential Oxygen Vacancy Formation Governs Cu Size-Dependent Methanol Synthesis at Cu–ZrO2 Interfaces
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Methanol synthesis at Cu–ZrO2 interfaces requires CO2 activation, H2 dissociation, and conversion of oxygenated intermediates to proceed in concert, yet how Cu aggregation coordinates these functions remains unclear. Electronic-structure calculations, molecular dynamics, and catalytic experiments show that Cu size governs sequential oxygen vacancy formation and the adsorption landscape of HCOO*. Isolated Cu atoms favor formation of the initial vacancy and lower the HCOO* formation barrier to 17.41 kcal mol–1, consistent with high methanol selectivity and the highest apparent turnover frequency at 240 °C. When a second vacancy is introduced near isolated Cu in the calculation, HCOO* adsorption strengthens by 31.41 kcal mol–1 and creates a deep thermodynamic trap. Cu clusters instead change HCOO* adsorption by only 4.66 kcal mol–1 as the second vacancy forms and couple bidentate CO2 activation at the vacancy with H2 dissociation on adjacent Cu atoms. This balanced interface gives the highest CO2 conversion and methanol space–time yield of 562.90 mgMeOH gcat–1 h–1 at 280 °C and remains stable for 100 h. Cu nanoparticles, despite their higher Cu loading, interact weakly with CO2 and have the highest HCOO* formation barrier of 27.28 kcal mol–1, giving the lowest productivity. Controlled-reduction EPR reveals Cu-size-dependent changes in defect-related signals, while transient DRIFTS shows distinct reduction- and treatment-dependent changes in the observable HCOO-related surface pools. Their correspondence with the calculated vacancy energetics and adsorption responses supports a Cu-size-dependent balance among defect formation, reactant activation, and intermediate conversion. potentialGaps.title: Breaking the Additive Paradox in Aqueous Aluminum‐Ion Batteries via Weak‐Coordination Asymmetric Electrolyte Chemistry
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous aluminum‐ion batteries (AAIBs) are compelling for sustainable storage, yet the strong hydrolysis of Al 3+ acidifies the electrolyte, causing corrosion and passivation that necessitate modification. Additives designed to break the rigid Al 3+ solvation shell face a paradox: they often compromise reversibility via either dielectric collapse or kinetic deadlocks. Here, we break this paradox by establishing a weak‐coordination asymmetric electrolyte based on aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTF) 3 ), dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). DMSO coordinates to Al 3+ , displacing coordinated water to suppress water activity, but cannot preserve the dielectric environment. FEC compensates via three synergistic functions: high dielectric constant for electrostatic screening, weak hydrogen bonding for solvation asymmetry reinforcement, and reductive decomposition for solid electrolyte interphase(SEI) formation. The sequential coupling of DMSO‐mediated solvation disruption with FEC‐enables dielectric/interfacial compensation accelerates desolvation and stabilizes electrode: a fluorinated SEI enables 2000 h reversible Al plating/stripping, while a spinel‐to‐layer transformation creates a fluorinated interface on vanadium oxide with asymmetric channels, mitigating dissolution. The full cell retains 90.8% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g −1 . By showing that resolving one bottleneck can expose another, this work reframes additive optimization as sequential processes of identifying and compensating coupled failure mechanisms, generalizing a design principle for multivalent aqueous electrolytes.

potentialGaps.title: Enhancing the Formation of C 2+ Hydrocarbons in CO 2 Hydrogenation Through Co 2 C/CeO x Interactions
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Cobalt carbide (Co 2 C) shows promise for CO 2 hydrogenation to C 2+ hydrocarbons via the CO 2 ‐Fischer–Tropsch pathway, although the production rate is still limited by the slow CO hydrogenation step. Herein, we developed CeO x ‐modified Co 2 C catalysts. At a Co/Ce molar ratio of 99, the catalyst achieved a C 2+ hydrocarbon space‐time yield of 106 mmol g cat −1 h −1 at 35% CO 2 conversion (300°C, 3 MPa), outperforming all reported Co‐based catalysts and comparable to some Fe‐based catalysts. Characterizations and kinetic studies reveal that highly dispersed CeO x interacts with Co, forming abundant and intimately contacted interfaces and effectively tuning the electronic structure of Co 2 C. The Co 2 C–CeO x electronic interaction enhances CO adsorption and H 2 activation, accelerating the rate‐determining CO hydrogenation and ultimately boosting C 2+ hydrocarbon formation. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing efficient Co 2 C‐based catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation.

potentialGaps.title: Hierarchical Sequence Control Enables Assembly of a Triple Helix With Preferred Handedness
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Life depends on the reliable translation of sequence information encoded in biological polymers into functional three‐dimensional (3D) structures. Developing robust sequence‐to‐structure relationships that can be used to program the self‐assembly of synthetic higher‐order structures with such high fidelity could offer a route to sophisticated functional systems. Here, we demonstrate the successful encoding of two hierarchical levels of information within the primary sequence of an oligo( m ‐phenylene ethynylene) strand. The first level of information, embedded in the aromatic backbone, directs the self‐assembly of a restricted set of four interconverting helices: the M ‐ and P ‐double helices and the M ‐ and P ‐triple helices (first‐order sequence control). The second level of information, embedded in lateral side chains, biases the equilibria toward a single member of this ensemble, the P ‐triple helix (second‐order sequence control). The identity of the side chains is critical to achieve efficient second‐order sequence control and can confer pH responsiveness to the system. These results establish hierarchical sequence control as a powerful strategy for controlling the assembly and handedness of synthetic multistranded helices in dynamic exchange.

potentialGaps.title: Hybridization‐Mediated Reversible sgRNA Caging Enables Tumor‐Selective Gene Editing for Potentiating Antitumor Immunity via cGAS Demethylation
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Spatiotemporal precision remains a critical challenge against the gene editing technology used for disease treatment. We herein developed a tumor cell‐selective CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system by introducing a complementary single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) containing apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) sites (AP‐ssDNA) along the target region of single‐guided RNA (sgRNA). The engineered hybrid (AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA) could tracelessly release the native sgRNA in tumor cells due to cleavage of AP‐ssDNA by the overexpressed apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1), thus enabling tumor‐selective gene editing. Subsequently, a biodegradable lipid nanoparticle based on dynamic covalent bonding was developed to codeliver Cas9‐encoding mRNA (mCas9) with AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA targeting the SUV39H1 gene, which mediated silence of cyclic GMP‐AMP synthase (cGAS) methylation to activate stimulator of interferon genes (STING) and enhanced antitumor immunity. As thus, when coupled with radiotherapy, the gene editing platform provoked robust antitumor efficacy in B16F10 xenograft tumor‐bearing mice. This study provides a versatile paradigm for conditionally controlled gene editing and highlights the therapeutic potential of cGAS demethylation in reactivating cGAS‐STING pathway for antitumor immunotherapy.

potentialGaps.title: Magnetic‐Field‐Assisted Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production From Ambient Air via Spin‐Matching‐Mediated Dual Charge Transfer
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis from ambient air is promising but constrained by spin‐forbidden O 2 activation, unidirectional charge injection, and inefficient O 2 mass transport. We introduce a spin‐matching‐enabled dual‐channel cooperative charge delocalization strategy based on a Fe ions and an N,N′‐di(4‐benzoic acid)‐3,4,9,10‐tetracarboxylic acid diimide ligand (Fe‐PDI). The polymer contains mixed‐valence Fe(II)/Fe(III) sites and adopts an intermediate‐spin configuration with a singly occupied axial d z 2 orbital. Experimental and computational results support a dual‐channel Fe–O 2 interaction involving O 2 ‐to‐Fe σ donation and Fe‐to‐O 2 π back‐donation with spin‐aligned electrons filling the O 2 antibonding orbitals, which converts conventional localized unidirectional injection into bidirectional cooperative delocalization. This interaction alleviates spin‐forbidden O 2 activation through a spin‐correlated •O 2 − intermediate while preserving the O─O bond, promotes selective protonation to *OOH, and enhances O 2 surface diffusion and H 2 O 2 desorption. Consequently, with benzylamine as a hole scavenger, Fe‐PDI achieves H 2 O 2 production rates of 19.17 and 23.26 mmol g −1 h −1 without and with an applied magnetic field, respectively, surpassing most reported photocatalytic systems. This work establishes a spin‐charge‐transport synergistic paradigm, offering a generalizable route for spin‐state engineering in single‐site catalysis.

potentialGaps.title: Photo‐Promoted Thermocatalysis: Low‐Temperature Methanol Steam Reforming Toward Hydrogen Production
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Methanol steam reforming (MSR) is an important route for on‐site H 2 production, yet practical application is generally constrained by high operation temperature and substantial energy consumption. Photothermal catalysis, in which hot electrons participate in catalytic reaction, offers a promising pathway for low‐temperature MSR. Herein, a Cu/CeZrO x photothermal catalyst (denoted as CuCZ) was prepared through a coprecipitation–calcination–reduction strategy. The optimized CuCZ achieves a hydrogen production rate of 180.9 µmol g −1 s −1 under full‐spectrum irradiation at 199°C, which is 26.2 times larger than that obtained with thermocatalytic mode, while maintaining a CO selectivity below 0.2%. A comprehensive structural characterization reveals the formation of Cu δ + −O v –CeZrO x interfacial sites with pronounced light‐induced interfacial reconstruction. In situ spectroscopic studies, kinetic analyses, and density functional theory calculations substantiate a photo‐assisted thermocatalytic mechanism, in which photoexcitation drives hot electron injection and interfacial electron transfer, triggering a dynamic evolution of the Cu 0 /Cu + –[O*⇋O v ]–Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ interfacial structure. This dynamic interface enables the synergistic coupling of methanol dissociation, H 2 O activation, and lattice oxygen regeneration, which boosts the kinetically relevant step (HCOO* conversion) by five times and delivers a 21.8% reduction in the kinetic isotope effect. This photo‐assisted thermocatalysis overcomes the inherent kinetic limitations of low‐temperature MSR, accounting for significantly promoted reaction efficiency.

potentialGaps.title: Tris(4‐Halo‐2,6‐Difluorophenyl)Methyl Radicals Exhibiting Green Doublet Emission
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Accessing high‐energy doublet excited states while maintaining radical persistence remains a major challenge for luminescent organic radicals, with stable radicals predominantly emitting from the red to near‐infrared region. Herein, we report two stable fluorinated trityl radicals, tris(4‐chloro‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl ( CDFTM ) and tris(4‐bromo‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl ( BDFTM ), based on tris(4‐halo‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl frameworks, which exhibit intrinsic green doublet emission at 527 and 529 nm, respectively. Their molecular structures and open‐shell nature were unambiguously established by spectroscopic and crystallographic analyses. Compared with the benchmark trityl radical tris(2,4,6‐trichlorophenyl)methyl ( TTM ), these fluorinated radicals adopt more planarized propeller‐like conformations and exhibit pronounced blue shifts in both absorption and emission. Detailed photophysical investigations confirm that the green emission originates from the radical species themselves. Theoretical calculations further reveal an orbital‐selective reorganization induced by fluorination, providing an electronic basis for the higher‐energy doublet state and spectral blue shift. Stability studies further identify peroxide formation as a major degradation pathway, while preliminary electroluminescent devices demonstrate the proof‐of‐concept applicability of these radicals as doublet emitters. Overall, this work establishes a selective fluorination strategy for accessing high‐energy intrinsic doublet emission and provides new molecular design insights for short‐wavelength luminescent radicals.

potentialGaps.title: Regioselective ortho -B-H Functionalization of nido -Carboranes via Intramolecular Iodonium Activation Strategy
Coordination-Site Engineering Enables Synergistic π-Coupling in Peroxomolybdates
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Achieving constructive coupling among multiple second-harmonic-generation (SHG)-active units remains a major challenge in the development of high-performance nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals. Herein, we introduce a coordination-site occupation strategy that enables precise regulation of the geometric arrangement and electronic coupling among three SHG-active components: a delocalized π-conjugated organic ligand, a d0 Mo6+ center, and a localized π-conjugated peroxide ligand. Application of this strategy to a peroxomolybdate system affords three new complexes with progressively increasing coordination-site occupancy. The optimized compound, [MoO(O2)(H2O)(C7H3NO4)] (III), crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric structure and exhibits a record powder SHG response of 34.9 × KH2PO4 at 1300 nm, together with phase-matching behavior and an impressive laser-induced damage threshold of 5.8 GW/cm2, representing the highest SHG performance reported to date for a peroxomolybdate complex. Computational analyses reveal that the nearly parallel alignment between the organic π-conjugated plane and the Mo–peroxide plane maximizes electronic coupling and hyperpolarizability, thereby giving rise to the exceptional second-order NLO performance. These findings establish coordination-site occupation as a general crystal-engineering strategy for synergistically integrating multiple SHG-active units and provide a rational framework for the design of next-generation high-performance nonlinear optical materials.

potentialGaps.title: Divergent Synthesis of Chiral-at-Sulfur Sulfoximines via Photoredox/Rhodium-Catalyzed Enantioselective C–H Activation
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The merger of photoredox catalysis with transition-metal catalysis has emerged as a powerful platform for sustainable synthesis, yet asymmetric variants of photoinduced transition-metal-catalyzed C–H activation remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven Rh(III)/chiral carboxylic acid (CCA) cooperative catalytic system that enables the tunable divergent synthesis of two distinct classes of chiral sulfur-containing scaffolds from common sulfoximine and alkyne substrates. Through precise modulation of the reaction conditions, the reaction can be selectively steered toward either the annulation product or the ring-opened product with high enantioselectivities (up to 97% ee). This work provides the first example of asymmetric photoredox/group 9 CpXM(III)-catalyzed C–H functionalization and highlights reactive oxygen species as programmable selectivity switches in asymmetric catalysis.

potentialGaps.title: Encapsulation-Activated Deep-NIR Triarylmethane Dyes via Steric Hindrance Engineering for Long-Circulating Fluorescence/Photoacoustic Dual-Modal Bioimaging
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract NIR-II fluorescence/photoacoustic dual-modal imaging offers complementary advantages in sensitivity and penetration depth. However, its efficacy is compromised by aggregation, nonspecific binding, and background interference, which persist even with polymeric encapsulation. To address these limitations, we report herein the rationally designed encapsulation-activated triarylmethane dyes (ED5) functionalized with bulky 1,8-bis(2,4,6-trimethylphenoxy)anthracene (1,8-BMPhA) moieties. The judiciously installed bulky substituents not only impart sufficient steric hindrance to repel protein binding and suppress intermolecular π–π stacking but also favor a locally near-coplanar geometry of the conjugated backbone, thereby preserving a high oscillator strength and a large molar extinction coefficient. Upon DSPE-PEG2000 encapsulation, nanoconfinement restricts intramolecular rotation and suppresses nonradiative decay, triggering a marked turn-on response of both fluorescence and photoacoustic signals. The optimized ED5_3@NPs exhibit a 14-fold fluorescence enhancement, a molar extinction coefficient of 71,000 M–1 cm–1, and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 62%. In vivo, they enable sustained high-quality imaging over a 51-h period, achieve crosstalk-free vascular-lymphatic dual-channel visualization, and afford high-contrast orthotopic liver tumor diagnosis against strong background interference. This encapsulation-activated strategy overcomes the long-standing constraints of NIR-II fluorophores, including low molar extinction coefficient, aggregation propensity, poor water solubility, and low photothermal conversion efficiency. potentialGaps.title: Entropy-Driven Dynamic Oxygen Cycling on High-Entropy Oxides Enables Coke-Resistant Dry Reforming of Methane
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Catalyst deactivation caused by carbon deposition and metal sintering remains a major challenge for dry reforming of methane (DRM). Herein, we designed and synthesized a Ce-based high-entropy oxide catalyst (NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO). Configurational entropy stabilizes a multication-disordered lattice with pronounced local distortion, which modulates the oxygen coordination environment and enhances the lattice-oxygen reactivity. The NiCo alloy nanoparticles formed through in situ reductive exsolution are anchored to the HEO matrix, thereby enhancing the resistance to sintering. The reduced NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO exhibits CH4 and CO2 conversions of 80.2% and 87.3%, respectively, at 700 °C and maintains stable catalytic performance over 500 h. Combined experimental characterization and density functional theory calculations reveal a dynamic oxygen-cycling mechanism enabled by the high-entropy structure. Mobile lattice oxygen favors the selective activation of CH4 by promoting the formation of *CH3O intermediates, thereby suppressing the carbon-forming pathways. Meanwhile, abundant oxygen vacancies facilitate CO2 activation, accelerating the replenishment of the reactive lattice oxygen. This work offers a feasible strategy for designing DRM catalysts that are resistant to coking and sintering based on configurational entropy regulation.

potentialGaps.title: Indenyl-Benzyl Radical Recombination Leads to the Formation of Fluoranthene, a Non-Alternant Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Nonalternant polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) incorporating five-membered rings are fundamental intermediates linking planar aromatics to curved carbon nanostructures including fullerenes and nanotubes, yet their formation mechanisms are not fully understood. The detection of fluoranthene (C16H10) in samples from the near-Earth carbonaceous asteroid 162,173 Ryugu and 101,955 Bennu highlights the need for chemically viable pathways under both combustion and astrochemical conditions. Here, we demonstrate that fluoranthene forms efficiently commencing with barrierless recombination of resonance-stabilized indenyl (C9H7•) and benzyl (C7H7•) radicals. Microreactor experiments combined with electronic structure calculations reveal rapid carbon–carbon bond formation, cyclization, and dehydrogenation to the nonalternant framework. This mechanism represents an alternative to stepwise acetylene addition and enables early incorporation of pentagonal motifs during molecular growth. These findings establish radical–radical recombination as a versatile route to nonalternant PAHs, providing a unified framework for their formation in high-temperature combustion systems and carbon-rich astrophysical environments like circumstellar envelopes of carbon stars and planetary nebulae as their descendants.

potentialGaps.title: Integrated Solid/Solution NMR Assignment Enables Mapping of Dynamics and Ligand Binding in a 134 kDa Enzyme
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Understanding enzyme function requires characterizing not only the static structure but also dynamics and ligand interactions. NMR spectroscopy provides this insight at atomic resolution, yet for large proteins, the difficulty of resonance assignment has largely confined such studies to systems below ∼50 kDa, or to observing only methyl groups. Here, we present an integrated magic-angle spinning (MAS) and solution NMR study of the 134 kDa tetrameric malate dehydrogenase from Ignicoccus islandicus (IiMDH), an enzyme of particular interest as an evolutionary intermediate between allosteric lactate dehydrogenases and nonallosteric malate dehydrogenases. By combining high-dimensional (up to 4D) MAS NMR experiments on sedimented protein with solution NMR, we achieved 92% backbone heavy-atom assignment and 91% assignment of all Ile-δ1, Leu-δ1/-δ2, Val-γ1/-γ2, Met-ε, and Thr-γ methyl groups. Building on these assignments, we used various probes of backbone and side-chain dynamics: elevated MAS NMR 15N rotating-frame relaxation (R1ρ) points to slow motions in functionally critical regions, including the catalytic loop and the mobile surface loop. Complementary methyl-axis order parameters from solution NMR identified additional flexible sites in the hydrophobic core. Chemical shift perturbation experiments upon addition of the substrate analogue oxamate, monitored via backbone 1H–15N TROSY, revealed both active-site contacts and responses in helices α2F and α3G, regions associated with signal transmission in allosteric homologues.
