potentialGaps.title: Linkage-Engineered Fabrication of a Robust 1,6-Anthrazoline-Linked Covalent Organic Framework with Significantly Promoted Exciton Dissociation for Superior Photocatalysis
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising polymeric photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen evolution, yet their performance is often hampered by tightly bound excitons that suppress efficient charge separation. Herein, we present a linkage engineering strategy that directly attenuates excitonic effects through a facile two-step postsynthetic protocol combining imine bond locking with site-specific protonation. This approach affords a new class of readily functionalizable 1,6-anthrazoline-linked COFs (TP-PACOFs) featuring cationic, fully conjugated backbones with high planarity, tunable donor–acceptor character, and well-preserved crystallinity. Such a structurally synergistic design enables the cyano-containing derivative, TP-PACOF-CN, to overcome the “trade-off” barrier among synthetic accessibility, light-harvesting capability, exciton binding strength, surface wettability, and chemical stability. Strikingly, TP-PACOF-CN achieves a benchmark sacrificial photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate of 307.8 mmol g–1 h–1 under visible-light irradiation, which is 1.9 times higher than that of its biquinoline-linked analogue and surpasses nearly all reported COF-based photocatalysts. Moreover, it delivers an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 31.6% at 420 nm, retains activity up to 700 nm (AQY = 1.9%) and exhibits excellent recyclability. Comprehensive spectroscopic investigations and theoretical simulations demonstrate that the ingenious architectural motif of TP-PACOF-CN significantly promotes exciton dissociation and facilitates charge-carrier dynamics. This work provides valuable insights into exciton management in organic semiconductors and underscores the potential of structurally engineered COFs for high-efficiency solar fuel production.

potentialGaps.title: Migratory Hydroamination of Alkenes via Iron-Hydride Catalysis
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The renaissance of catalytic metal hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT) offers advanced tools for hydroamination of alkenes. Despite these merits, state-of-the-art MHAT hydroamination protocols are largely limited to intermolecular coupling or intramolecular cyclization, thereby necessitating new catalytic platforms to explore MHAT reactivity and access unexplored hydroamination reaction pathways. Herein, we report an iron hydride-catalyzed migratory hydroamination of allylamines, enabled by a sequential MHAT process with finely tuned 1,2-amino migration. This strategy converts readily accessible allylamines into structurally diverse alkylamines and β-amino acids through a three-step radical cascade. This protocol features a broad tolerance toward a range of functional groups, encompassing complex drug and natural product derivatives. Beyond providing an efficient approach to medicinally relevant amine scaffolds, this work establishes a new paradigm for MHAT-enabled molecular editing through radical functional group migration, thereby expanding the synthetic repertoire of alkene hydroamination.

potentialGaps.title: Probing the Conformational Behavior of a Seven Hetero-Spin Supramolecule
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The synthesis and crystal structure of a 7-spin supramolecular poly-rotaxane is reported. The [4]rotaxane structure involves a trigonal thread centred on a {CrNi2} core, with each of the three arms terminated by Cu(II) centres and bearing a {Cr7Ni} metallocycle. The macromolecule brings together three distinct electron spin centers. Continuous-wave electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy confirms the molecule remains intact in solution, with the three types of spin center each uniquely addressable. Orientation-selective Double Electron Electron Resonance (DEER) and Relaxation Induced Dipolar Modulation Enhancement (RIDME) spectroscopies are used to selectively probe the different spin-spin interactions in the frozen solution phase and to define differences from the solid-state crystal structure.

potentialGaps.title: Resination-Assembled Soft Multiaxial Molecular Ferroelectrics Enable Exceptional Low-Electric Field Polarization Switching
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Resination of soft polymer ferroelectrics has recently emerged as a promising avenue to assemble high- performance electroactive materials, due to the coupling of ferroelectricity with enhanced mechanical and processable merits. However, it remains a huge challenge to stabilize ferroelectricity and dipolar activity at the resin–ferroelectric interface. For the first time, we adopt here the resination assembling strategy into the soft molecule-based ferroelectric (BZA)2(DMA)BiI6 (1, BZA = benzylammonium; DMA = dimethylammonium), which enables the unusual ferroelectric behavior of low-electric field switching of polarization. Compound 1 is a high-temperature multiaxial ferroelectric with six possible equivalent polarization directions and a low coercive electric field, arising from its stepwise phase transitions around 350 K (Tc). Strikingly, the precise resination of 1 with the epoxy-matrix composite yields a highly loaded composite with a microscopic cross-linked structure, whose polarization can be switched under a quite low coercive electric field (Ec ∼ 3.8 kV/cm). These shape-customized ferroelectric resin wafers of 1 have superior antielectric fatigue attributes after ∼104 cycles. Moreover, these wafers exhibit enhanced resistance to localized deformation, evidenced by a 30.9% decrease in maximum penetration depth relative to the bulk single crystals. As the first study on the resination of molecular ferroelectrics, our findings bridge the gap between molecular ferroelectrics and material engineering, which highlights the application potential of resinated molecular ferroelectrics.

potentialGaps.title: Substrate Length Controls Atropopeptide Complexity and Triggers Excision-Driven Scaffold Hop to Diketopiperazine Alkaloids
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Atropopeptides are a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that share conserved cross-link-forming amino acids in their core peptides, yet adopt architectures ranging from simple monocyclic to complex polycyclic structures with intriguing three-dimensional shapes. These complex architectures arise from multiple C–C and C–N cross-links that are installed by a single cytochrome P450 enzyme, but the factors governing these divergent cross-linking patterns and resulting structural complexities have remained elusive. Recent studies on RiPP biosynthesis have revealed a form of substrate-controlled catalysis, in which the precursor sequence, rather than the modifying enzyme, dictates the reaction course. Here, we describe a distinct form of substrate-controlled catalysis in atropopeptide biosynthesis, demonstrating that core peptide length, rather than sequence, determines the cross-linking pattern installed by an atropopeptide-forming cytochrome P450. We further uncover an unusual proteolytic excision of an internal amino acid in mature atropopeptides, generating peptides that spontaneously convert into pyrroloindoline-containing diketopiperazines (DKPs) and thereby effecting a nonenzymatic scaffold-hop from atropopeptides to DKP-derived alkaloids, for which we provide mechanistic insight. Both the atropopeptide and the corresponding DKP exhibit antiviral activity, and their structural diversity can be further expanded through precursor engineering. Our work reveals substrate length as a key determinant of atropopeptide complexity, provides insights into the catalysis of a multicross-link-forming P450, and establishes an unprecedented route connecting atropopeptides to pyrroloindoline DKP alkaloids.

potentialGaps.title: π-Armor: Shape-Complementary Encapsulation of Aromatics
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Host–guest binding can be classified into two well-separated modes, i.e., reversible binding under thermodynamic control and permanent encapsulation via kinetic trapping during host formation. However, combining both modes within a single π-conjugated host on the basis of host–guest shape complementarity has remained challenging. Here, we present the design and synthesis of a neutral D3-symmetric π-conjugated cage (1), wherein two curved hexa-cata-hexabenzocoronene (c-HBC) panels are bridged by dibenzodiazocine (DBDA) units to form three orifices and a biconvex nanocavity. Cage 1 reversibly encapsulates aromatic guests, whereby binding affinities are governed by dispersion arising from shape complementarity. In contrast, bulky guests that are too large to pass through the orifices are incorporated during cage formation and permanently entrapped, affording thermally robust carceplexes. Even a π-extended guest exceeding the cavity size was entrapped, with its aryl groups protruding through the three orifices to form a mechanically interlocked molecule. Thus, cage 1 behaves as a dual-mode host controlled by shape complementarity, representing a “π-armor” that sandwiches aromatic guests between its π-surfaces.

potentialGaps.title: MPAThio Ligand-Accelerated Palladium-Catalyzed Nondirected Hydrogen Isotope Exchange of Arenes with D2O
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen isotope exchange is an atom-economical strategy for accessing deuterium-labeled molecules, but its synthetic utility is often limited by slow exchange kinetics and poor reactivity of π-extended arenes. Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed nondirected hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) enabled by a dual-ligand combination of a monoprotected aminoethyl thioether (MPAThio) and an N-heteroarene ligand. This system exhibits faster HIE kinetics, reaching isotopic equilibrium within 30 min at 105 °C (and within 60 min at 90 °C), and enables efficient deuterium incorporation under mild conditions using D2O as the deuterium source. The protocol enables efficient deuteration of a broad range of mono- and multisubstituted arenes. For poorly soluble substrates relevant to organic light-emitting diode materials, a cosolvent strategy addresses solubility limitations, affording high deuterium incorporation. Mechanistic studies indicate that the MPAThio ligand lowers the barrier of accessing the reactive C–H activation manifold, thereby favoring efficient reversible HIE.

potentialGaps.title: Photochemical Radical Cascade Annulation of 6-Azauracils Enabled by CsPbBr3 Perovskite Nanocrystals
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Direct annulation of 6-azauracils has remained challenging due to their strongly electron-deficient and decomposition-prone heterocyclic frameworks. This study presents unique insight into the core modification of the 6-azauracil system enabled by a CsPbBr3 perovskite nanocrystal-promoted photochemical cascade cyclization with an amino acid derivative. N-Phenylglycine, a zwitterion with strong surface binding affinity for the photocatalyst, generated a nucleophilic aminomethyl radical in dimethyl carbonate that added to the C═N bond, triggering a radical cascade to tetrahydroimidazole-fused triazines, structures of emerging relevance in biochemical applications. Dimethyl carbonate ensured radical stability and catalyst integrity, enabling a broad scope and late-stage functionalization. Beyond azauracils, the strategy also supports the late-stage functionalization of a range of biologically important drug molecules, providing a cost-effective, sustainable, and operationally simple platform for light-mediated synthesis empowered by perovskite nanocrystals.

potentialGaps.title: Synthesis of Pyrido[2,3- d ]pyrimidin-4(3 H )-ones via SNAr/Tandem Cyclization
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract A new method has been developed for constructing the pyrido[2,3-d]pyrimidin-4(3H)-one scaffold under metal- and ligand-free conditions. In this strategy, 2-bromo-N-phenylnicotinamide is activated by the synergistic electron-withdrawing effects of the pyridine ring and the amide group, enabling tandem nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr)/cyclization with cyanamide or formamide under simple conditions. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support an SNAr/cyclization mechanism. Preliminary photophysical studies show that the products exhibit blue emission, suggesting potential applications in materials science. Additionally, molecular docking studies indicate that the synthesized scaffold may have relevance to medicinal chemistry, providing a foundation for future biological evaluations.

potentialGaps.title: Selective, Catalytic Oxidation of Polyethylene Surfaces
Epitaxial-strain engineering of supported tensile noble metallene oxides for enhanced oxidation catalysis
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO 2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO 2 and rutile SnO 2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO 2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO 2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO 2 . The tensile-strained PtO 2 /SnO 2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt–O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO 2 , delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T 90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO 2 /TiO 2 and 469 °C for PtO x /Al 2 O 3 ) and 1% conversion loss over 38 h under both dry and wet conditions. Moreover, this epitaxial strain strategy is generalizable to other environmentally relevant oxidation reactions and rutile-type noble metal oxides, establishing tensile strain imposed by epitaxial lattice matching as a general principle for stabilizing atomically thin noble metal oxides while tuning their electronic structure.

potentialGaps.title: Gamma-alumina as a highly active hydrogenation catalyst deciphered by molecular nitrogen
Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode–skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

potentialGaps.title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.

potentialGaps.title: A general synthesis of tryptophan-crosslinked macrocyclic peptides enabled by a dual-functional directing group
Synthesis of chiral allylic amines through regio- and enantioselective homologation of enamines using Ni catalysis
Bioinspired Total Syntheses of Tricrilactones D and F, Crispatumine I, and 2,3- trans -Crispatumine I
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The bioinspired total syntheses of tricrilactones D and F, crispatumine I, and 2,3-trans-crispatumine I are reported. The conserved lactone-fused 9/5/6 spirocyclic core of these products was constructed via a mild bioinspired one-pot three-component cascade of protrilactione A, the purported biosynthetic precursor. Variation of the aldehyde and β-ketolactone components enable access to both homo- and heterocoupled natural products, each in 13 steps (longest linear sequence).

potentialGaps.title: Calix[n]BODIPYs: One-Pot Assembly of Strain-Relieved Methylene-Bridged Macrocycles with Bright Fluorescence
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract We report a mild, one-pot synthetic approach to a family of β,β′-methylene-bridged all-BODIPY macrocycles (Calix[n]BODIPYs). Key to our design is a β-hydroxymethyl-functionalized BODIPY precursor: upon activation by BF3·OEt2, the in situ generated benzylic carbocation undergoes sequential Friedel–Crafts-type alkylation at the β-positions of adjacent BODIPY units. These macrocycles exhibit strong intramolecular excitonic coupling, exceptionally high molar extinction coefficients (up to 7.39 × 105 M–1·cm–1), and bright fluorescence (ΦFL up to 0.92).

potentialGaps.title: Construction of Difluoro-Functionalized Heterocycles via Annulation and Concomitant Fluorine Incorporation
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a novel cascade annulation strategy for the expedient synthesis of difluoro-functionalized quinolines and quinoxalines. This protocol is compatible with both 2-aryl and 2-vinyl anilines, enabling the controllable incorporation of various fluorine-containing functionalities, including CF2H, SCF2H, and SeCF2H. For CF2H installation, the annulation of 2-aryl/vinyl anilines with BrCF2CO2Et was developed, in which BrCF2CO2Et serves as a C1 building block and a difluorocarbene precursor. Notably, in the presence of external sulfur or selenium sources, a one-pot reaction with S/Se and BrCF2CO2Et was realized, providing a diverse array of valuable fluoromethylthio(seleno)-functionalized N-heterocycles under metal-free conditions. Furthermore, the direct introduction of the SCF2H moiety into quinoxalines was achieved via difluoromethyl thiolation under the same reaction conditions.

potentialGaps.title: Deacylative Functionalization of Ketones via Radical-Triggered Alkyl–Acyl Bond Cleavage
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Herein, we disclose a radical-triggered deacylative functionalization of ketones that proceeds efficiently under transition-metal-free and high-energy-light-free conditions. Readily accessible methyl ketones are harnessed to form pre-aromatic intermediates (PAIs), which undergo aromatization-promoted α-C–C bond scission to deliver versatile carbon-centered radicals. Leveraging this radical intermediate, a diverse range of deacylative reactions, including alkenylation, alkynylation, heteroarylation, and oxime etherification, were successfully achieved.

potentialGaps.title: In Situ Cyclization/Reduction of Polynitro Azides into Insensitive High-Energy Compounds
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Polynitro azide compounds have attracted considerable attention owing to their high energy content and large positive heats of formation. However, excessive sensitivity to external stimuli severely limits their practical application. Therefore, it remains a formidable challenge to reduce its sensitivity so as to enhance the safety. In this work, we report an in situ cyclization/reduction strategy that enables effective desensitization of polynitro azide compounds while preserving their high energy output, thereby affording a new class of insensitive high-performance energetic materials. Notably, the in situ cyclization effectively transforms the azide and trinitromethyl moieties into a fused ring system; the underlying mechanism is investigated in detail. All of the newly synthesized compounds exhibit good energetic properties.

potentialGaps.title: Manganese-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of α-Substituted Tetralones via Dynamic Kinetic Resolution
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Developing earth-abundant metal catalysts as alternatives to precious metals is highly appealing for asymmetric hydrogenation. However, low enantioselectivity and activity remain critical challenges. Herein, we disclose an efficient manganese-catalyzed asymmetric hydrogenation of α-substituted tetralones via dynamic kinetic resolution. A wide range of chiral tetrahydronaphthols containing two contiguous stereogenic centers were obtained in high yields and stereoselectivities (up to 99% yield, 99% ee, and gt;20:1 dr). The practicality of this protocol was demonstrated by a gram-scale synthesis of the key intermediate of (+)-elacestrant, a therapeutic agent for metastatic breast cancer, at a catalyst loading of 0.0038 mol %, with a TON (26 000) that was significantly higher than that achieved with the precious-metal catalysts for this hydrogenation.

potentialGaps.title: Photocatalyzed Trifluoromethylamidative Ring Opening of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes: Access to Trifluoromethylamidyl Cyclobutenes
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The trifluoromethylamination method has recently evolved as a powerful paradigm for preparing N-CF3 compounds, among which the NCF3 radical-transfer approach is of particular interest but remains underdeveloped. Here we report a photocatalyzed trifluoromethylamidative ring-opening reaction of donor–acceptor bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs), delivering a range of inaccessible but valuable trifluoromethylamidyl cyclobutenes. The method expands the heteroatom-radical-mediated ring-opening reaction of BCBs and enables radical trifluoromethylamination at sp3 carbon, thereby challenging current addition reactions of NCF3 radical only with unsaturated molecules.

potentialGaps.title: A Z‐Scheme CuWO 4 /Poly(heptazine imide) Interface Coupled With Asymmetric Cu 2+ /Cu + Sites Enables Efficient Photocatalytic CO 2 ‐to‐Ethanol Conversion
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective photocatalytic reduction of CO 2 into multicarbon products remains challenging because constructing uniform C─C coupling centers while maintaining their stability under reaction conditions is difficult. Here, we report a Z‐scheme CuWO 4 /poly(heptazine imide) heterojunction featuring asymmetric Cu 2+ /Cu + dual sites for CO 2 ‐to‐ethanol conversion. Site‐selective oxygen vacancies in CuWO 4 trigger generation of structurally identical, charge‐asymmetric neighboring Cu sites, which enhance CO 2 activation and stabilize adjacent *CO intermediates, thereby facilitating C─C bond formation. Meanwhile, an atomically bonded O─W─N heterointerface enables directional Z‐scheme charge transfer, supplying photogenerated electrons to the CuWO 4 surface and stabilizing the asymmetric Cu 2+ /Cu + dual sites throughout photocatalysis. Consequently, the optimized photocatalyst achieves an ethanol production rate of 244.5 µmol g −1 h −1 in pure water without sacrificial reagents. Advanced synchrotron spectroscopies identify the asymmetric Cu 2+ /Cu + dual sites and the chemically bonded heterointerface, while operando spectroscopies record the dynamic evolution of active sites and the * CO─ * CO coupling pathways upon illumination. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the synergy between asymmetric catalytic centers and the atomically bonded heterointerface promotes the C─C coupling process. This work establishes a strategy for constructing and stabilizing asymmetric catalytic centers through atomic engineering of crystal structure and heterointerface, providing a photocatalyst design paradigm for selective multicarbon solar fuel synthesis.

potentialGaps.title: Bifunctional Metal–Organic Frameworks Integrate Energy‐ and Electron‐Transfer Pathways for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanophotosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT), but most reported systems rely predominantly on a single O 2 ‐activation pathway, limiting their ability to produce complementary reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a bifunctional MOF, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, that integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers (DBP) and viologen electron mediators (VIO 2+ ) within a single framework to establish a dual‐channel photoactive platform. The close spatial proximity of these two functional units enables efficient intra‐framework electron transfer while preserving the energy transfer capability of the porphyrinic photosensitizers. Upon 630 nm irradiation, excited DBP transfers electrons to VIO 2+ to generate viologen radical species, which mediate O 2 reduction to generate type I ROS, including superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals. The resulting DBP radical cation is reduced by endogenous biomolecules such as 1,4‐dihydronicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, thereby regenerating DBP and sustaining the photoredox cycle. Concurrently, energy transfer from excited DBP to O 2 produces singlet oxygen through a type II pathway. Compared with the viologen‐free MOF analogue, Hf‐VIO‐DBP markedly enhances type I ROS generation while retaining efficient type II ROS production, resulting in substantially improved overall ROS yields and phototoxicity. Therefore, Hf‐VIO‐DBP achieves potent PDT efficacy in CT26 and MC38 murine colon cancer models.

potentialGaps.title: Carbodicarbene σ/π‐Donation Enables a Reactive Two‐Coordinate Germanium(II) Dication
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT All previously reported Ge(II) dications have remained chemically dormant, their reactivity confined to simple coinage metal coordination—a consequence of cationization‐induced lone pair contraction that renders the Ge center inaccessible to substrates. We report that dual σ/π‐donating carbodicarbene (CDC) ligands directly counteract this contraction, yielding [(CDC) 2 Ge][OTf] 2 ( 4 ), the first two‐coordinate Ge(II) dication to display broad reactivity beyond coinage metal coordination. Crystallographic and computational analysis reveal a delocalized 3c‐4e C‐Ge‐C moiety and a less contracted Ge lone pair with retained Ge‐centered LUMO, underpinning an unprecedented reactivity profile encompassing 1,1‐oxidative addition, [1 + 4] cycloaddition, selenium insertion, and cooperative C–S bond activation. As a Ge‐donor ligand, 4 coordinates to Rh, Ir, and Ag with donor strength comparable to that of IMes and forms geminal bimetallic complex 8 , featuring a rare noncluster Ag–Ge–Ag three‐center two‐electron bonding motif. These results establish CDC‐based low‐coordination stabilization as a productive strategy for accessing structurally simple yet reactive main‐group dications.

potentialGaps.title: Cerium Valence‐Gated Interfacial Exciton Reconstruction for Fluorescence Modulation
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial electronic coupling plays a decisive role in governing excited‐state evolution and signal transduction in optoelectronic systems, yet dynamically adaptive interfaces driven by valence‐state evolution remain largely unexplored in fluorescent sensing platforms. Herein, an Eu‐functionalized Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface is constructed to establish a valence‐responsive optoelectronic system for dual‐mode H 2 O 2 sensing. Upon oxidative stimulation, the Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface dynamically reconstructs the interfacial charge‐transfer network through Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ valence‐state evolution, enabling modulation of electron migration across the interface and synchronously regulating Eu‐centered luminescence, CTF‐derived fluorescence, and nanozyme‐mediated catalytic outputs. The results reveal that oxidative valence evolution induces adaptive interfacial electronic redistribution and excited‐state pathway reconstruction, thereby amplifying microscopic electronic perturbations into programmable fluorescence–catalytic responses. Beyond conventional sensing systems dominated by static emissive centers, this work demonstrates that adaptive interface states can function as dynamic optoelectronic units for intelligent signal transduction. Furthermore, the interfacial optical response can be integrated into flexible electrospun membranes and machine‐learning‐assisted visual recognition systems, enabling portable dual‐mode visual sensing. This work provides a new perspective for constructing adaptive optoelectronic interfaces through valence‐state engineering and establishes a general framework for next‐generation intelligent sensing platforms.

potentialGaps.title: Charge‐Delocalizing sp‐Hybridized COFs for Selective H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is an important oxidant for chemical manufacturing, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications, yet its industrial production still relies mainly on the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Electrochemical H 2 O 2 synthesis via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) provides a sustainable alternative but is often hindered by sluggish charge transport and insufficient O 2 activation. Here, we develop a bond‐hybridization strategy by incorporating sp‐hybridized acetylene units into the vertex or linker of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). The resulting COFs feature extended π‐conjugation, enhanced charge delocalization, and electronically polarized pores, thereby strengthening O 2 adsorption and activation. Compared with sp 2 ‐dominated analogues, these sp‐hybridized COFs show faster charge‐transfer kinetics, higher H 2 O 2 selectivity, and improved 2e − ORR activity. In a flow cell, the optimized catalyst delivers an H 2 O 2 production rate of 27.8 mol g −1 h −1 and a peak Faradaic efficiency of 91.7% at 150 mA cm −2 . Mechanistic analyses combining electronic‐structure calculations and in situ vibrational spectroscopy reveal that sp hybridization reshapes frontier‐orbital distributions and local charge density, thereby coupling framework‐wide charge delocalization with favorable O 2 adsorption and *OOH stabilization. These results establish bond hybridization as a molecular‐level design parameter for catalytic selectivity in COFs, extending framework engineering beyond conventional functional‐group and building‐block modification.

potentialGaps.title: Controlled Presodiation of Sodium‐Ion Cathode via Electron Cloud Engineering
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical presodiation offers a promising pathway to compensate sodium deficiency in cathode and anode materials, thereby enhancing the usable energy density of sodium‐ion batteries. This approach is particularly critical for P2‐ and tunnel‐type cathodes, such as Na 0.44 MnO 2 , where the as‐synthesized materials typically exhibit a 50%–60% sodium deficiency. However, conventional presodiation reagents possess excessively high reductive potential, often leading to oversodiation, structural degradation, and compromised electrode reversibility. Here, we report a rational electron‐cloud engineering strategy to precisely control the sodium chemical potential of presodiation agents. Guided by Hückel's rule, we demonstrate that tailoring π‐conjugation size and introducing electron‐withdrawing groups enables the adjustment of sodium chemical potential via a balance of conjugative and inductive effects. We identify 1‐indanone as an optimal presodiation reagent, capable of delivering sodium to Na 0.44 MnO 2 cathodes without any oversodiation. The resulting electrodes exhibit fully restored sodium inventories, an unprecedented first‐cycle Coulombic efficiency of ∼100%, and improved capacity retention over 350 cycles compared to untreated controls. Our findings establish a versatile framework for controlling sodium delivery in chemical presodiation, providing a new avenue for the design of next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries with enhanced stability and performance.

potentialGaps.title: Discovery of a Potent and Selective First‐In‐Class Antagonist of GPR15 With In Vivo Anti‐Obesity Activity
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT GPR15 (G Protein‐coupled Receptor 15), an atypical chemokine receptor, is implicated in the pathogenesis of multiple diseases, yet small‐molecule GPR15 antagonists remain undeveloped. Herein, we identify and characterize YL410 , the first‐in‐class potent and selective GPR15 antagonist. In the cAMP‐GloSensor assay, YL410 inhibits GPR15 with an IC 50 of 0.027 ± 0.005 µM, and displays high selectivity against a panel of related GPCRs and kinases. It suppresses GPR15L‐induced Jurkat T‐cell migration, and exhibits favorable pharmacokinetics and acceptable safety. Molecular docking, replicated molecular dynamics simulations, quantitative contact analyses, and mutagenesis experiments support a plausible orthosteric binding model for YL410 , maintained by a reproducible network of polar and hydrophobic contacts, which rationalizes its potent antagonism and observed structure–activity relationships (SAR). Complementary AI‐based structure predictions (AlphaFold3, Chai‐1, and Boltz) recapitulated the energetically accessible orthosteric poses but not the dynamically stable pose selected by the MD simulations, underscoring the importance of kinetic‐stability validation in antagonist pose selection. Notably, in a diet‐induced obesity (DIO) mouse model, YL410 administration induced significant weight loss and exerted blood glucose‐lowering effects. Collectively, this study presents the first potent, selective, and in vivo efficacious GPR15 antagonist, providing new insights into the development of therapeutics for the treatment of obesity.

potentialGaps.title: Double‐Volcano Catalytic Response in Furfural Reductive Amination Over Inverse Ni─Al Catalysts
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Reductive amination of aldehydes and ketones to primary amines is an important route for biomass valorization, yet achieving efficient synergy between substrate and hydrogen activation in cascade reactions remains challenging. Herein, we construct a compositionally tunable Ni─Al catalyst system whose architecture evolves from conventional Ni/Al 2 O 3 to inverse Al 2 O 3 /Ni. This structural evolution gives rise to an unusual double‐volcano catalytic behavior in furfural reductive amination. Two activity maxima are identified over 30Ni/Al 2 O 3 and inverse Al 2 O 3 /90Ni, respectively, with the optimal Al 2 O 3 /90Ni catalyst delivering 98.5% furfurylamine yield and a space‐time yield of 65 mmol g cat −1 h −1 under mild conditions. Adsorption studies, initial‐rate kinetic isotope effect and reaction‐order measurements, apparent activation‐energy analysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy indicate that the double‐volcano behavior reflects the coupled evolution of catalyst composition and architecture and a composition‐dependent balance between Lewis‐acid‐assisted intermediate formation and hydrogen‐dependent intermediate conversion. Hydrogen‐dependent steps exert a stronger kinetic influence over 30Ni/Al 2 O 3 than over Al 2 O 3 /90Ni, while the inverse catalyst exhibits enhanced H 2 adsorption and activation and more rapid Schiff base conversion. These results indicate a shift in the dominant kinetic limitation between the two catalysts and provide a framework for designing efficient non‐noble‐metal catalysts for multifunctional cascade reactions involving coupled substrate and hydrogen activation.

potentialGaps.title: Engineering Polar Nanoregions in COFs via Controlled Symmetry Breaking Toward Piezocatalysis
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT To address the limited piezocatalytic activity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) arising from high structural symmetry and rapid charge recombination, an imine‐linked COFs (TFB‐TAPT) is synthesized by Schiff‐base condensation of 1,3,5‐triformylbenzene (TFB) and 2,4,6‐tri(4‐aminophenyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TAPT), followed by partial substitution of amino ligands with 1H,1H‐undecafluorohexylamine (UFHA) through a building‐block exchange strategy to afford TFB‐TAPT‐FA. This approach achieves controlled symmetry breaking with precise polar group distribution, without the lattice disruption caused by asymmetric monomers in one‐pot methods. The resulting randomly oriented polar nanoregions exhibit relaxation behavior, collectively generating a strong piezoelectric response under external stimuli. Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) measurements indicate that TFB‐TAPT‐FA has a piezoelectric coefficient of 140 pm/V, 2.5 times that of TFB‐TAPT. This amplification of the electromechanical response arises from the polar nanoregions, as evidenced by its higher calculated dipole moment (5.68 Debye). Consequently, TFB‐TAPT‐FA achieves an impressive piezocatalytic hydrogen production rate of 3.8 mmol g −1 h −1 , marking a 17‐fold improvement over TFB‐TAPT. Notably, TFB‐TAPT‐FA enables efficient hydrogen production without cocatalysts or heterojunctions. More broadly, the introduction of polar nanoregions similarly enhances the performance of other imine‐linked COFs, demonstrating a potentially general strategy for designing piezocatalysts through nanoscale polarization engineering in COFs.

potentialGaps.title: Hydroxyl Regulation Enables Metal Promoter‐Free Iron Catalysts for Highly Efficient CO 2 Hydrogenation to Light Olefins
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT The efficient hydrogenation of CO 2 to light olefins over Fe‐based catalysts typically relies on the metal promoters, such as alkali or transition metals. In this study, we find that the intrinsic hydroxyl environments may be the crucial but long‐overlooked factor governing the activity of Fe species. With the assistance of low‐concentration guar gum, hydrogen‐bond networks formed by dense hydroxyls are disrupted to generate isolated or terminal hydroxyl groups, which increase the active sites and significantly facilitate the product desorption. The resulting metal promoter‐free Fe achieves a CO 2 conversion of 30.1% and a light olefin selectivity of 38.1% at an ultra‐high gas hourly space velocity of 300 000 mL g cat −1 h −1 . Meanwhile, the space‐time yield of light olefins reaches 3.3 kg kg cat −1 h −1 , which outperforms all of the reported Fe‐based catalysts modified by various promoters. These findings redefine hydroxyls as intrinsic promoters in Fe catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation and can potentially be extended to other heterogeneous catalytic systems and reactions.

potentialGaps.title: In Situ Metal Chelation for Topology Regulation and Single‐Site Construction in Covalent Organic Frameworks
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise regulation over the dimensionality and topology of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through metal coordination remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report an in situ metal‐chelation strategy for topology regulation and single‐site construction in COFs using a bifunctional β ‐hydroxy ketone‐functionalized HDBC monomer. Metal‐free Schiff‐base condensation of HDBC with TAPy affords a one‐dimensional covalent ribbon framework, named COF‐HDBC. Strikingly, in situ Cu 2+ chelation during solvothermal crystallization redirects the assembly pathway toward a two‐dimensional bex ‐type Cu‐COF‐HDBC containing framework‐embedded Cu─O coordination sites. Post‐synthetic metalation of preassembled COF‐HDBC fails to trigger this transformation, verifying the indispensable structure‐directing effect of in situ chelation during nucleation and growth. This strategy is extendable to Ni 2+ and Co 2+ , affording isostructural metal‐chelated COFs. Multiscale characterizations and Cu K‐edge XAFS collectively support the proposed framework structures and the predominantly isolated nature of the Cu centers. As a functional validation, Cu‐COF‐HDBC enables selective CO 2 /CO electroreduction to CH 4 . This work establishes in situ metal chelation as a synthetic handle for programming COF topology and constructing framework‐embedded single‐metal sites, offering a versatile route to crystalline porous materials with complex architectures and tunable functions.

potentialGaps.title: Mixed‐Valence Dimeric Olympicenyl Radical Cation With Improved Electrical Conductivity
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT p‐Type doping is an effective strategy for modulating molecular packing arrangement of organic compounds, thus improving their electrical conductivity. In this work, the first example of a mixed‐valence radical cation dimer based on an odd alternant hydrocarbon, [OR5] 2 +• [FeCl 4 ] − (OR5‐MV), was successfully prepared by the oxidation of olympicenyl radical (OR) derivative OR5 using FeCl 3 . X‐ray crystallographic analysis revealed that cation‐radical dimer [OR5] 2 +• , acting as a fundamental building block, forms [OR5] 4 2+ tetramer via a multi‐center–two‐electron bond, which further aggregates into a one‐dimensional chain in the solid state. SQUID measurement reveals that the magnetic susceptibility is dominated by the FeCl 4 – anions with no detectable OR5 moiety contribution. Theoretical calculations disclosed an open‐shell singlet ground state for [OR5] 4 2+ tetramer and demonstrated that the pancake‐bond formation between OR5 cation‐radical dimers confers significant energetic stabilization. Compared to the neutral compound, more uniform molecular packing and reduced intermolecular distance in the one‐dimensional columnar architecture of OR5‐MV facilitate effective intermolecular orbital overlap, leading to broader band dispersion along the molecular stacking direction. A substantially improved electrical conductivity of up to 10 − 3 S cm − 1 is achieved compared to neutral radical (10 − 9 S cm − 1 ), representing the highest value reported for monomeric odd alternant hydrocarbons.

potentialGaps.title: Proximity‐Engineered Dual‐Atomic Cobalt Sites Enable Adaptive Spin Catalysis for Simultaneous Oxygen and Peroxide Reduction
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Breaking the intrinsic adsorption conflicts among oxygen intermediates remains a central challenge in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) electrocatalysis. Although spin‐state engineering offers an effective strategy for tuning catalytic activity, conventional approaches generally focus on a single‐spin configuration, which cannot simultaneously satisfy the distinct energetic requirements of different ORR intermediates. Here, we introduce an adaptive spin catalysis concept through proximity engineering of dual‐atomic Co sites confined within a one‐dimensional covalent organic framework. Precisely regulating the Co–Co separation while preserving the local coordination environment induces inter‐site electronic coupling, giving rise to coexisting high‐spin and low‐spin Co configurations. Combined spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations support a mechanistic framework in which these coexisting spin configurations provide complementary catalytic functions for distinct intermediates along the multistep ORR pathway, thereby alleviating adsorption conflicts. Consequently, the proximity‐engineered catalyst delivers outstanding ORR activity with a half‐wave potential of 0.96 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, outperforming both its spatially separated counterpart and commercial Pt/C. The catalyst also efficiently mediates both O 2 and H 2 O 2 reduction while suppressing peroxide decomposition, enabling enhanced performance in rechargeable zinc–air batteries and peroxide‐assisted aluminum–air batteries. This work establishes a molecular framework for exploiting spin‐state complementarity in atomic catalysts for advanced energy‐conversion reactions.

potentialGaps.title: Tailoring Backbone Angles of Regioisomeric Covalent Organic Frameworks: Distinct O 2 Adsorption Modes Enabling Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) possess periodic skeletons and well‐defined catalytic sites, allowing precise molecular‐level regulation of interfacial properties in electrocatalytic oxygen reduction. However, conventional structural modifications fail to systematically tune oxygen adsorption geometry and interfacial electronic coupling. Here, we report a linkage‐angle engineering strategy that alters the bonding positions of reactive aldehyde groups to fabricate three regioisomeric COFs with predefined backbone dihedral angles of 180°, 120°, and 60°. The angle‑driven regioisomeric effect induces considerable differences in dipole moments together with uneven charge distribution. These collective structural features remodel oxygen‑surface interactions and modulate the intrinsic catalytic kinetics. Theoretical calculations confirm that the compact 60° framework of o ‐TPDA‐COF reconstructs confined pore interfacial microenvironments. Unlike the Griffiths‑type oxygen adsorption favored in its angular analogues, molecular oxygen preferentially adopts the Pauling configuration within o ‐TPDA‐COF to stabilize OOH* intermediates. Consequently, the optimal o ‐TPDA‐COF reaches an excellent H 2 O 2 productivity of 12.82 mol g cat −1 h −1 and a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 91.64%. This work realizes controllable modulation of oxygen‑adsorption behaviors in COF‑based 2e – oxygen reduction, delivering a novel geometry‑oriented design paradigm for porous electrocatalytic frameworks.

potentialGaps.title: Solvent Control of Cheletropic Recombination in Benzosultine-Derived ortho -Quinodimethane Diels–Alder Reactions
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Thermolysis of benzosultines generates ortho-quinodimethanes (o-QDMs) widely used in Diels–Alder (DA) chemistry, yet productive cycloaddition is often limited by rapid cheletropic SO2 recombination to form benzosulfolenes. Combined computational and experimental studies support a model in which benzosultine thermolysis proceeds through kinetically competent o-QDM/SO2 encounter complexes positioned at the boundary between pericyclic and open-shell reactivity. Although reversible C–S homolysis accounts for efficient TEMPO trapping, stereochemical probe experiments establish that productive cycloaddition proceeds through a concerted DA pathway. The absence of o-QDM dimerization indicates that free o-QDM does not accumulate under the reaction conditions, leading to an apparent mechanistic paradox: how can intermolecular cycloaddition compete with rapid cheletropic SO2 recombination? The combined computational and experimental data are most consistent with a model in which DA reactions occur within the same solvent cage as competing SO2 recombination. As a result, cheletropic SO2 recombination is highly medium sensitive: replacing aromatic solvents such as toluene with nonpolar aliphatic hydrocarbons markedly suppresses benzosulfolene formation and reverses product selectivity in favor of productive DA cycloaddition. These findings establish solvent-controlled encounter-complex partitioning as a general strategy for improving benzosultine-derived o-QDM cycloadditions.

potentialGaps.title: Plant invasions are associated with lower community stability at multiple spatial scales
potentialGaps.abstract: Plant invasions are threatening the long-term sustainability of ecosystem functions. Yet, how plant invasions impact the temporal stability of community cover across spatial scales remains poorly understood, hindering effective invasion management. Using the National Ecological Observatory Network dataset, we examine how plant invasions influence multi-scale stability of total community abundance (used total community cover) via altering community functional diversity, as well as growth and dispersal strategies. We find that invasion-associated losses of functional α diversity and functional shifts toward acquisitive strategies, reduce species asynchrony and species stability, respectively. These changes ultimately lead to lower temporal stability at the local scale (α stability). Meanwhile, invasion-associated functional shifts toward acquisitive seed dispersal strategies weaken functional β diversity, which reduces asynchrony community dynamics among local communities (spatial asynchrony). These concurrent declines in α stability and spatial asynchrony collectively destabilize metacommunity-scale stability. Our findings reveal that plant invasions may trigger destabilizing effects across spatial scales, associated with changes in functional diversity as well as growth and dispersal strategies, underscoring the need for a multi-scale invasion management framework focusing on both local diversity and the connectivity among local communities. Plant invasions can threaten ecosystems by making plant communities less stable over time. The study shows that invasions reduce stability from local to metacommunity scales by eroding functional diversity and favoring fast-growing strategies.

potentialGaps.title: Targeting MDA5 induces immunogenic cell death and promotes anti-tumor immunity
potentialGaps.abstract: Identifying targets to enhance tumor immunity is an urgent need. Although nucleic acid sensors play critical roles in promoting tumor immune clearance, their exceptionally low mutation rate in cancers suggests potential unexplored roles in tumor progression. Here, we demonstrate that the RNA sensor melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA5) promotes immune evasion, and its high expression is strongly predictive of poor survival and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy in patients. Targeting MDA5 reshapes the tumor microenvironment, strengthening immune memory responses and enhancing effector CD8⁺ T cell activity in preclinical models in female mice. Mechanistically, MDA5 deficiency triggers unfolded protein response driven immunogenic cell death through induction of damage-associated molecular patterns, leading to enhanced dendritic cell-mediated antigen engulfment and T cell activation. Additionally, MDA5 loss primes the ASK1-JNK/P38 signaling pathway, sensitizing tumor cells to TNF-α/IFN-γ, further amplifying this process. Consequently, targeting MDA5 enhances the efficacy of ICB therapy across multiple cancer types, positioning it as a promising therapeutic target. RNA sensors have been linked to antitumor immune responses. Here, based on results of in vivo CRISPR screens, the authors propose the RNA sensor MDA5 as a regulator of immune evasion, showing that its targeting induces immunogenic cell death and anti tumor immunity.
